overall.assessment: Prema dostavljenom tematskom prikazu, podcast snažno njeguje molitvu, pobožnost, nadu u svetost i razmatranje blaženstava, što je u osnovi usmjereno prema Kristu i skladu je s kršćanskim životom. Ipak, spoj tvrdnji o osobnom viđenju anđela, sotonskom djelovanju, neimenovanoj anđeoskoj „pusti nečega iz ruke” i nemirima u Europi, uz pozivanje na Gospine poruke i „Božji ustanak”, stvara rizik da se privatna tumačenja predstave kao pouzdan ključ za čitanje političkih i povijesnih događaja. Ta napetost između evanđeoske pobožnosti i apokaliptično-političkog uokvirivanja snižava ukupnu procjenu; iz samog sažetka ipak nije moguće utvrditi točne formulacije, namjeru govornika ni je li izrečena tvrdnja predstavljena kao privatno mišljenje ili kao crkveno potvrđena objava.
seeds_of_logos: Molitve Božjem milosrđu, krunica i zazivi Mariji mogu podržati pouzdanje u Boga i predanje Kristu; pobožnosti su dobro usmjerene kada ostaju u skladu s javnom Objavom i vode k Kristu.
Razmatranje blaženstava i svetosti na svetkovinu Svih svetih stavlja naglasak na put Isusova učenika, a ne samo na izvanredne pojave; papa Franjo blaženstva opisuje kao put koji vodi susretu s Bogom.
Naglasak na radosti, nadi i dostojanstvu vjernika kao Božje djece ima biblijsko uporište u 1 Iv 3,2 i odgovara kršćanskoj nadi koja ne poriče patnju, nego vjernike usmjerava prema Bogu.
Promicanje javnog djelovanja vjernika može biti pozitivan poticaj ako služi općem dobru i pravima svake osobe, a ne političkom mobiliziranju koje druge prikazuje kao neprijatelje.
concerns: Osobno viđenje anđela povezano s tumačenjem nemira u Europi može slušatelje navesti da spekulativnu interpretaciju prihvate kao objavljenu činjenicu. Crkveni kriterij za privatne objave jest sukladnost s javnom Objavom i usmjerenost Kristu; navodna proroštva treba razborito provjeravati, a ne graditi na njima alternativni plan spasenja ili sigurnost o budućim događajima.

Govori o „Sotoni koji rešeta Crkvu”, nebeskim silama i „Božjem ustanku” mogu, ako nisu pažljivo razjašnjeni, pojačati strah i podjelu ili sakralizirati politički odnosno nacionalni projekt. Kršćansko čitanje znakova vremena treba voditi obraćenju, nadi i ljubavi, a djelovanje u javnosti mjeriti služenjem osobi i općem dobru.

Molitva oslobođenja može biti izraz povjerenja u Božju zaštitu, ali iz sažetka nije razvidno razlikuje li se jasno molitveni zaziv od službenog obreda egzorcizma niti potiče li se slušatelje na strah od zlih sila. Također, sama obrana od optužbi u vezi s donacijama ne omogućuje zaključak o njihovoj istinitosti; u crkvenim inicijativama važni su odgovornost i transparentnost.
overall.theological_context: Biblijski okvir svetkovine čine blaženstva (Mt 5,1–12) i nada da smo Božja djeca (1 Iv 3,2): svetost se prepoznaje u putu koji vodi Kristu, a ne u senzacionalnim tumačenjima događaja. Dokument Zbora za nauk vjere o poruci Fatime i smjernice za razlučivanje navodnih ukazanja ističu da privatne objave ne nadomještaju javnu Objavu te ih treba razlučivati prema nauku, duhovnim plodovima i crkvenom prosuđivanju. Socijalni nauk, kako je ovdje izražen u Christifideles Laici i Caritas in veritate, vrednuje javno sudjelovanje prema služenju osobi, pravdi, općem dobru i odgovornosti, a ne prema strahu ili neprovjerenim političkim proročanstvima.

overall.assessment_en: According to the provided thematic overview, the podcast strongly fosters prayer, devotion, hope in holiness, and meditation on the beatitudes, which is fundamentally oriented toward Christ and in harmony with Christian life. Nevertheless, the combination of claims about a personal vision of angels, satanic action, an unnamed angelic "release of something from the hand" and unrest in Europe, along with invoking Our Lady's messages and a "God's uprising," creates a risk that private interpretations are presented as a reliable key for reading political and historical events. This tension between evangelical devotion and apocalyptic-political framing lowers the overall assessment; however, from the summary itself it is not possible to establish the exact formulations, the speaker's intention, nor whether the stated claim was presented as a private opinion or as an ecclesially confirmed revelation.
overall.theological_context_en: The biblical framework of the solemnity consists of the beatitudes (Mt 5:1–12) and the hope that we are children of God (1 Jn 3:2): holiness is recognized on the path that leads to Christ, and not in sensational interpretations of events. The document of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith on the message of Fatima and the guidelines for the discernment of alleged apparitions emphasize that private revelations do not replace public Revelation and must be discerned according to doctrine, spiritual fruits, and ecclesial judgment. Social doctrine, as expressed here in Christifideles Laici and Caritas in veritate, evaluates public participation according to service to the person, justice, the common good, and responsibility, rather than according to fear or unverified political prophecies.
seeds_of_logos_en: Prayers to Divine Mercy, the Rosary, and invocations to Mary can support trust in God and surrender to Christ; devotions are well-directed when they remain in harmony with public Revelation and lead to Christ.

Meditation on the beatitudes and holiness on the Solemnity of All Saints places emphasis on the path of Jesus' disciple, rather than merely on extraordinary phenomena; Pope Francis describes the beatitudes as a path that leads to an encounter with God.

The emphasis on joy, hope, and the dignity of believers as children of God has a biblical foundation in 1 Jn 3:2 and corresponds to Christian hope that does not deny suffering, but directs believers toward God.

Promoting the public action of believers can be a positive encouragement if it serves the common good and the rights of every person, rather than political mobilization that portrays others as enemies.
concerns_en: A personal vision of angels associated with the interpretation of unrest in Europe may lead listeners to accept a speculative interpretation as a revealed fact. The ecclesial criterion for private revelations is conformity with public Revelation and orientation toward Christ; alleged prophecies should be prudently examined, rather than building an alternative plan of salvation or certainty about future events upon them.

Talk about "Satan sifting the Church," heavenly powers, and a "God's uprising" can, if not carefully clarified, heighten fear and division or sacralize a political or national project. A Christian reading of the signs of the times should lead to conversion, hope, and love, and action in public should be measured by service to the person and the common good.

A prayer of deliverance can be an expression of trust in God's protection, but from the summary it is not evident whether a prayerful invocation is clearly distinguished from the official rite of exorcism, nor whether listeners are encouraged to fear evil powers. Also, the mere defense against accusations regarding donations does not allow a conclusion about their truthfulness; in church initiatives, responsibility and transparency are important.

sections.subtitle: Svetkovina Svih Svetih počinje pozivom na radost
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Vladimir Grebenar pozdravlja gledatelje i slušatelje medija Ora et Labora i čita redak iz evanđelja dana
sections.content:
Epizoda broj 125 medija Ora et Labora, naslovljena **„Milosrđe Božje – Svetkovina Svih Svetih!“**, počinje kratkim pozdravom. Voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** obraća se „dragim gledateljima i slušateljima medija Ora et Labora“. Odmah zatim donosi redak iz evanđelja dana: **„Radujte se i kličite, velika je plaća vaša na nebesima.“**

Te riječi iz Isusova govora o blaženstvima određuju ton cijele emisije. Govore o radosti i nadi u nebesku nagradu, što pristaje svetkovini na kojoj Crkva slavi sve one koji su tu nagradu već primili.

Nakon pozdrava slijedi znak križa: „U ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga. Amen.“ Time počinje opsežan molitveni dio koji traje gotovo trideset sedam minuta. Obuhvaća:

- molitve zaštite i oslobođenja,
- molitve posvete,
- Krunicu Božjeg milosrđa,
- Litanije Božjem milosrđu,
- Gospinu krunicu sa slavnim otajstvima,
- završnu molitvu „Zdravo Kraljice“.

Voditelj sve molitve izgovara sam. Velik dio tekstova napisan je u množini („nas“, „naše obitelji“), pa molitva od početka uključuje cijelu zajednicu onih koji je prate.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je usklađen s katoličkim naukom: blaženstvo i obećanje nebeske nagrade primjereno su povezani sa Svetkovinom Svih Svetih, a zajednička molitva odražava crkveni karakter vjere. Navedeni sadržaj ne pokazuje očit teološki problem.
magisterium.enrichment: Svetkovina Svih Svetih ne slavi samo nebesku nagradu nego i Božje djelovanje u svetima, koji su vjernicima uzori i zagovornici. Blaženstva pozivaju i vjernike na zemlji da slijede Krista i rastu u svetosti, pa radost zbog svetih ide zajedno s pozivom na vjerno življenje Evanđelja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is aligned with Catholic teaching: beatitude and the promise of a heavenly reward are appropriately connected with the Solemnity of All Saints, and communal prayer reflects the ecclesial character of faith. The stated content does not show an obvious theological problem.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Solemnity of All Saints celebrates not only the heavenly reward but also God's action in the saints, who are role models and intercessors for believers. The beatitudes also invite believers on earth to follow Christ and grow in holiness, so joy because of the saints goes together with the call to live the Gospel faithfully.

sections.subtitle_en: The Solemnity of All Saints begins with a call to joy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Vladimir Grebenar greets the viewers and listeners of the media outlet Ora et Labora and reads a verse from the gospel of the day
sections.content_en:
Episode number 125 of the media outlet Ora et Labora, entitled **„Divine Mercy – Solemnity of All Saints!“**, begins with a brief greeting. Host **Vladimir Grebenar** addresses the „dear viewers and listeners of the media outlet Ora et Labora“. Immediately thereafter he presents a verse from the gospel of the day: **„Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven.“**

Those words from Jesus' discourse on the Beatitudes set the tone for the entire program. They speak of joy and hope in the heavenly reward, which suits the solemnity on which the Church celebrates all those who have already received that reward.

After the greeting follows the sign of the cross: „In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.“ With that begins an extensive prayer section that lasts nearly thirty-seven minutes. It encompasses:

- prayers of protection and deliverance,
- prayers of consecration,
- the Chaplet of Divine Mercy,
- the Litany of Divine Mercy,
- the Rosary of Our Lady with the glorious mysteries,
- the concluding prayer „Hail, Holy Queen“.

The host recites all the prayers alone. A large part of the texts is written in the plural („us“, „our families“), so from the beginning the prayer includes the entire community of those following along.

sections.subtitle: Molitva oslobođenja: vezivanje zlih sila i poziv nebeskim zaštitnicima
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj izgovara molitvu kojom u ime Isusovo vezuje zle sile i obitelji stavlja pod zaštitu Kristove krvi
sections.content:
Prva molitva u emisiji je molitva za oslobođenje i zaštitu. Voditelj počinje riječima: **„U ime Isusovo uzimam vlast i vežem sve zle sile i snage“**. Zatim nabraja gdje se te sile nalaze:

- u zraku,
- na zemlji,
- u vodi,
- u podzemlju,
- na onome svijetu,
- u prirodi,
- u vatri.

Nakon toga molitva se okreće slavljenju Boga: „Ti si Gospodin nad svim svemirom; dajem ti slavu u ime tvoga stvorenja.“ U ime Isusovo vezuju se „sve demonske sile koje su došle protiv nas i naših obitelji“. Svi koji mole stavljaju se pod zaštitu Kristove **„dragocjene krvi koja je prolivena za nas na križu“**.

U drugom dijelu molitva traži nebesku zaštitu. Od Marije, „naše majke“, moli se zagovor kod Presvetog Srca Isusova za sve obitelji, uz zaziv: **„Zaogrni nas svojim plaštem ljubavi, da se prestraši neprijatelj.“** Zatim se zazivaju sveti Mihovil i anđeli čuvari da „brane nas i naše obitelji u borbi protiv svega zla što obilazi svijetom“.

Vrhunac molitve je zapovijed: „U ime Isusovo zapovijedam svim silama i snagama zla da odstupe istog časa od nas, od naših domova i naše zemlje.“ Molitva završava zahvalom Isusu „jer si vjeran Bog i osjećaš s nama“.

### Molitva svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu

Odmah zatim, u 00:01:27, slijedi molitva svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu. Arkanđela se moli da „brani nas u boju protiv pakosti i zasjeda đavolskih“ i da bude „zaklon“. Naziva ga se **„vojvodom vojske nebeske“** i moli da „Sotonu i druge duhove zlobne koji svijetom obilaze na propast duša, božanskom krepošću i jakošću u pakao strovali“.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva za zaštitu od zla, zazivi Mariji, svetom Mihaelu i anđelima čuvarima te prośba oslonjena na Kristovu krv imaju jasne paralele u katoličkoj molitvenoj tradiciji, a molitva svetom Mihaelu gotovo doslovno slijedi odobreni tekst. Ipak, izraz „uzimam vlast i vežem sve zle sile” može ostaviti dojam da molitelj sam raspolaže vlasti nad demonima; katolički je jasnije moliti Boga da zaštiti i oslobodi, kako to naglašava i tekst molitve svetom Mihaelu: „May God rebuke him, we humbly pray.”
concerns: Formulacija „uzimam vlast” i zapovijed svim zlim silama da odmah odstupe mogu zamagliti razliku između prošnje Bogu za zaštitu i izravnog polaganja osobne vlasti nad zlim duhovima.

Nabrajanje zlih sila „na onome svijetu” i u različitim elementima prirode nije samo po sebi jasno proturječno katoličkom nauku, ali je teološki neodređeno i može poticati pretjerano usmjeravanje na demonsko.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija prepoznaje duhovnu borbu i molitvu za zaštitu, ali kršćanska sigurnost počiva na Bogu, a ne na posebnoj moći samog molitelja; biskupski tekstovi, primjerice, upućuju na molitvu, znak križa i pouzdanje u Božju zaštitu. Molitva svetom Mihaelu također je snažan i prikladan zaziv, no njezin je ključni naglasak da zlo obuzda Božja vlast, a anđeli služe Božjem djelovanju.

Prayers for Immediate Protection From the Powers of Darkness

magisterium.assessment_en: Prayer for protection against evil, invocations to Mary, Saint Michael, and guardian angels, and a petition relying on Christ's blood have clear parallels in the Catholic prayer tradition, and the prayer to Saint Michael almost verbatim follows the approved text. Nevertheless, the expression "I take authority and bind all evil powers" may leave the impression that the person praying personally possesses authority over demons; it is Catholically clearer to pray to God to protect and deliver, as the text of the prayer to Saint Michael also emphasizes: "May God rebuke him, we humbly pray."
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition recognizes spiritual warfare and prayer for protection, but Christian certainty rests on God, and not on a special power of the one praying; episcopal texts, for instance, point to prayer, the sign of the cross, and trust in God's protection. The prayer to Saint Michael is also a powerful and appropriate invocation, yet its key emphasis is that evil is restrained by God's authority, and angels serve God's action.
concerns_en: The phrasing "I take authority" and the command to all evil powers to depart immediately can obscure the distinction between a petition to God for protection and the direct assumption of personal authority over evil spirits.

Listing evil powers "in the other world" and in various elements of nature is not in itself clearly contradictory to Catholic teaching, but it is theologically vague and may encourage an excessive focus on the demonic.

sections.subtitle_en: Prayer of deliverance: binding evil powers and invoking heavenly protectors
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recites a prayer by which in the name of Jesus he binds evil powers and places families under the protection of the blood of Christ
sections.content_en:
The first prayer in the program is a prayer for deliverance and protection. The host begins with the words: **„In the name of Jesus I take authority and bind all evil powers and forces“**. Then he lists where those powers are found:

- in the air,
- on the earth,
- in the water,
- in the underworld,
- in the other world,
- in nature,
- in fire.

After that, the prayer turns to praising God: „You are the Lord over all the universe; I give you glory in the name of your creation.“ In the name of Jesus, „all demonic forces that have come against us and our families“ are bound. All who pray place themselves under the protection of Christ's **„precious blood that was shed for us on the cross“**.

In the second part, the prayer seeks heavenly protection. From Mary, „our mother“, intercession is implored before the Sacred Heart of Jesus for all families, with the invocation: **„Clothe us with your mantle of love, so that the enemy may be terrified.“** Then Saint Michael and the guardian angels are invoked to „defend us and our families in the battle against all evil that roams the world“.

The climax of the prayer is the command: „In the name of Jesus I command all powers and forces of evil to depart immediately from us, from our homes, and from our land.“ The prayer ends with thanksgiving to Jesus „because you are a faithful God and feel with us“.

### Prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel

Immediately thereafter, at 00:01:27, follows the prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel. The Archangel is asked to „defend us in battle against the wickedness and snares of the devil“ and to be a „safeguard“. He is called the **„prince of the heavenly host“** and asked to, „by the divine power and strength, cast into hell Satan and all other evil spirits who prowl through the world seeking the ruin of souls“.

sections.subtitle: Jedinstvo s Isusom i posvete dvama Srcima
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj izgovara posvetu Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu
sections.content:
Nakon molitava zaštite emisija prelazi na molitve predanja i jedinstva. U 00:01:47 voditelj izgovara molitvu jedinstva s Isusom: **„Moj ljupki Isuse, neka naše noge zajedno hode, neka naše ruke budu skupljene u jedinstvu, neka naša srca kucaju zajedno“**. Molitva redom traži sklad duše, misli, sluha i pogleda: „neka naše uši zajedno slušaju tišinu, neka naši pogledi duboko prodru jedan u drugi“. Završava molbom da „naše usne zajedno mole da zadobijemo milosrđe od vječnoga Oca“.

### Posveta Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu

U 00:02:21 slijedi posveta Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu. Mariju se zaziva kao „majku i kraljicu“ i njezinu Srcu predaje se **„čitavo svoje biće, svoje misli, riječi i djela“**. Posveta traži da Marija raspolaže svime što molitelju pripada, „sada i u vječnosti“. Svrha je trostruka: „na hvalu i slavu Presvetoga Trojstva, za posvećenje Crkve i spasenje svega svijeta“.

U završnom dijelu posvete moli se pomoć da se živi „dostojno moga krsnog posvećenja“ i da se „neopozivo pripada svome Otkupitelju“. Molitelj traži i da, poput Marije, sluša poticaje Duha Svetoga, kako bi se u njemu i u svemu vršila volja Božja.

### Molitva Presvetom Srcu Isusovu

U 00:03:06 slijedi molitva Presvetom Srcu Isusovu, koje se naziva **„izvorom svakoga dobra“**. Molitva povezuje klanjanje, vjeru, ufanje, ljubav i kajanje za grijehe. Molitelj Isusu daruje „ovo moje siromašno srce“ i moli da ga učini „poniznim, strpljivim, čistim“. Traži zaštitu u opasnostima, utjehu u nevoljama i žalostima, zdravlje tijela i blagoslov rada. Molitva završava molbom za „milost svete smrti“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom snažno usklađen s katoličkom pobožnošću: predanje Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu shvaća se kao put koji vodi Kristu, a molitva Presvetom Srcu Isusovu iskazuje vjeru, ufanje, ljubav i kajanje. Molitvu jedinstva s Isusom valja razumjeti kao pjesnički izraz bliskosti i suobličenja Kristu, a ne kao doslovno stapanje osobe s Bogom.
concerns: Izraz da Marija raspolaže svime što pripada molitelju može biti nejasan ako bi se razumio kao da Mariji pripada božanska vlast ili da ona zamjenjuje Boga; u katoličkom smislu riječ je o povjerenju i predanju koje je usmjereno Kristu.
Izrazi o zajedničkom hodu, rukama i srcima s Isusom jesu pobožna metafora; ne bi ih trebalo tumačiti kao poistovjećivanje čovjeka s Kristom.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno učiteljstvo potvrđuje posvetu Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu, ali naglašava da ona naposljetku upućuje na Srce njezina Sina i da se živi kroz život milosti, molitvu, pokoru i kršćanske dužnosti. Osobna posveta Presvetom Srcu Isusovu prikladno potvrđuje krsno posvećenje; pobožnost Srcu Kristovu vodi zajedništvu s Trojstvom i nalazi svoje središte u Euharistiji.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly strongly aligned with Catholic devotion: surrender to the Immaculate Heart of Mary is understood as a path leading to Christ, and prayer to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus expresses faith, hope, love, and repentance. The prayer of unity with Jesus should be understood as a poetic expression of closeness and conformation to Christ, and not as a literal merging of the person with God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's Magisterium confirms consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, but emphasizes that it ultimately points to the Heart of her Son and is lived through a life of grace, prayer, penance, and Christian duties. Personal consecration to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus appropriately confirms baptismal consecration; devotion to the Heart of Christ leads to communion with the Trinity and finds its center in the Eucharist.
concerns_en: The expression that Mary disposes of everything that belongs to the person praying can be ambiguous if understood as though divine authority belongs to Mary or that she replaces God; in the Catholic sense, it is a matter of trust and surrender that is directed toward Christ.
Expressions about walking together, hands, and hearts with Jesus are a pious metaphor; they should not be interpreted as an identification of man with Christ.

sections.subtitle_en: Union with Jesus and consecrations to the Two Hearts
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recites the consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary
sections.content_en:
After the prayers of protection, the broadcast moves on to prayers of surrender and union. At 00:01:47 the host recites a prayer of union with Jesus: **„My lovely Jesus, may our feet journey together, may our hands be gathered in unity, may our hearts beat together“**. The prayer in turn asks for harmony of soul, thoughts, hearing, and sight: „may our ears listen to the silence together, may our gazes penetrate deeply into one another“. It concludes with a plea that „our lips pray together to obtain mercy from the eternal Father“.

### Consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary

At 00:02:21 follows the consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary. Mary is invoked as „mother and queen“ and to her Heart is surrendered **„one's entire being, one's thoughts, words, and deeds“**. The consecration asks that Mary dispose of everything that belongs to the person praying, „now and in eternity“. The purpose is threefold: „for the praise and glory of the Most Holy Trinity, for the sanctification of the Church, and the salvation of the whole world“.

In the concluding part of the consecration, help is sought to live „worthily of my baptismal consecration“ and to „belong irrevocably to my Redeemer“. The person praying also asks, like Mary, to listen to the promptings of the Holy Spirit, so that in him and in everything the will of God may be accomplished.

### Prayer to the Sacred Heart of Jesus

At 00:03:06 follows a prayer to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, which is called the **„source of every good“**. The prayer connects adoration, faith, hope, love, and contrition for sins. The person praying offers Jesus „this poor heart of mine“ and asks Him to make it „humble, patient, pure“. He asks for protection in dangers, consolation in afflictions and sorrows, health of body, and blessing of work. The prayer ends with a plea for the „grace of a holy death“.

sections.subtitle: Krunica Božjeg milosrđa: „Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci…“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj izgovara molitvu „Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv…“ na početku desetice Krunice Božjeg milosrđa
sections.content:
U 00:03:38 voditelj najavljuje: **„Slijedi krunica Božjega milosrđa.“** To je središnja molitva epizode, kojoj i naslov emisije daje ime „Milosrđe Božje“.

Krunica počinje uvodnim molitvama:

- **Oče naš**,
- **Zdravo Marijo**,
- **Vjerovanje**, isповijest vjere u Boga Oca Stvoritelja, u Isusa Krista „mučenog pod Poncijem Pilatom“, raspetog, umrlog, pokopanog i uskrslog, te u Duha Svetoga, svetu Crkvu katoličku, općinstvo svetih, oproštenje grijeha, uskrsnuće tijela i život vječni.

Svaka od pet desetica počinje istom molitvom prikazanja: **„Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv, dušu i božanstvo preljubljenoga Sina tvojega, Gospodina našega Isusa Krista, kao zadovoljštinu za grijehe naše i cijeloga svijeta.“**

Nakon toga deset puta se ponavlja zaziv: **„Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci, budi milosrdan nama i cijelome svijetu.“** Taj zaziv obilježava gotovo osam minuta emisije, od 00:05:23 do 00:11:30. Ponavljanje stvara ritam u kojem se jedna rečenica pretvara u ustrajnu molbu za milosrđe, i to ne samo za one koji mole nego za cijeli svijet.

Zaziv počiva na Kristovoj muci i sadrži dvije misli: grijeh je stvaran i zahtijeva zadovoljštinu, a Božje milosrđe dostupno je svakome po Sinovoj žrtvi.

magisterium.assessment: Opis Krunice Božjeg milosrđa u skladu je s katoličkom vjerom jer se oslanja na Kristovu muku i moli milosrđe za sve, a ne pripisuje spasenjsku moć samom ponavljanju molitve. Govor o zadovoljštini ispravan je ako se razumije da svaka molitvena zadovoljština vjernika sudjeluje u Kristovoj žrtvi i potpuno ovisi o njoj.
concerns: Tvrdnju da grijeh zahtijeva zadovoljštinu treba izraziti tako da se ne sugerira kako Kristova žrtva nije dovoljna ili da čovjek svojim djelima može neovisno otkupiti grijehe.
magisterium.enrichment: Novozavjetni temelj molitve jest Kristova žrtva za grijehe svijeta, koju vjernici zazivaju i kojoj se pridružuju, a ne ponavljaju kao novu ili zasebnu otkupiteljsku žrtvu. Crkveno učiteljstvo uči da sva vrijednost zadovoljštine počiva na jedinoj Kristovoj žrtvi, dok vjernici mogu sjediniti svoje molitve i život s njom; zaziv za cijeli svijet izražava univerzalni doseg Kristova otkupljenja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the Chaplet of Divine Mercy is in accordance with the Catholic faith because it relies on Christ's Passion and begs mercy for all, rather than attributing salvific power to the mere repetition of the prayer. Talk of reparation is correct if it is understood that every prayerful reparation of the faithful participates in Christ's sacrifice and depends completely upon it.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The New Testament foundation of the prayer is Christ's sacrifice for the sins of the world, which believers invoke and join in, and do not repeat as a new or separate redemptive sacrifice. The Church's Magisterium teaches that all value of reparation rests on the sole sacrifice of Christ, while believers can unite their prayers and lives with it; the invocation for the whole world expresses the universal reach of Christ's redemption.
concerns_en: The claim that sin requires reparation should be expressed so as not to suggest that Christ's sacrifice is insufficient or that man by his deeds can independently redeem sins.

sections.subtitle_en: Chaplet of Divine Mercy: „For the sake of His sorrowful Passion…“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recites the prayer „Eternal Father, we offer you the body and blood…“ at the beginning of a decade of the Chaplet of Divine Mercy
sections.content_en:
At 00:03:38 the host announces: **„Next is the Chaplet of Divine Mercy.“** That is the central prayer of the episode, which also gives the program its title „Divine Mercy“.

The Chaplet begins with opening prayers:

- **Our Father**,
- **Hail Mary**,
- **The Creed**, profession of faith in God the Father Creator, in Jesus Christ „suffered under Pontius Pilate“, crucified, died, buried, and risen, and in the Holy Spirit, the holy Catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting.

Each of the five decades begins with the same offering prayer: **„Eternal Father, we offer you the body and blood, soul and divinity of your dearly beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, in atonement for our sins and those of the whole world.“**

After that, the invocation is repeated ten times: **„For the sake of His sorrowful Passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world.“** That invocation marks nearly eight minutes of the broadcast, from 00:05:23 to 00:11:30. The repetition creates a rhythm in which a single sentence turns into a persistent plea for mercy, not only for those praying but for the whole world.

The invocation rests upon Christ's passion and contains two thoughts: sin is real and requires atonement, and God's mercy is available to everyone through the Son's sacrifice.

sections.subtitle: Od „Svetog Bože“ do litanija: trideset zaziva Božjem milosrđu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli Litanije Božjem milosrđu s ponavljanim odgovorom „uzdam se u tebe“
sections.content:
Krunica Božjeg milosrđa završava u 00:11:33 trostrukim zazivom: **„Sveti Bože, sveti jaki Bože, sveti besmrtni Bože, smiluj se nama i cijelome svijetu.“**

Zatim slijede zazivi uzdanja:

- „O krvi i vodo, što potekoste iz srca Isusova, kao izvor milosrđa za nas, uzdam se u tebe.“
- „Marijo, majko milosrđa, moli za nas.“
- tri puta ponovljeno **„Isuse, uzdam se u tebe.“**

### Litanije Božjem milosrđu

U 00:12:21 počinju Litanije Božjem milosrđu. Nakon uobičajenog uvoda („Gospodine, smiluj se. Kriste, smiluj se…“) i zaziva Presvetom Trojstvu slijedi dugi niz zaziva. Svaki počinje riječima „Milosrđe Božje“, a završava odgovorom **„uzdam se u tebe“**.

Zazivi prate povijest spasenja od stvaranja do vječnosti. Milosrđe se opisuje kao:

- „neshvatljiva tajna Presvetoga Trojstva“ i „izraz njegove najveće moći“,
- ono koje se objavilo „u stvaranju nebeskih duhova“ i koje „nas iz ništavila pozvalo u život“,
- ono koje „nas zaštićuje od zasluženih kazna“ i „oslobađa od bijede grijeha“,
- ono koje se „izlijeva iz rana Kristovih“ i „izvire iz Presvetoga Srca“,
- ono koje je „dalo Presvetu Djevicu za majku milosrđa“,
- ono vidljivo u ustanovljenju Crkve i sakramenata, „neograničeno u sakramentu krštenja i pokore“ i „neizmjerno u sakramentu oltara i svećeništva“,
- „vrelo bolesnicima i patnicima“, „ufanje onih koji očajavaju“ i „mir umirućih“,
- ono koje „olakšava patnje dušama u čistilištu“ i koje je „neizmjerna radost sviju svetih“,
- „neiscrpivi izvor čudesa“.

### Završna molitva

Litanije završavaju retkom: **„Bog je milosrdan i pun samilosti, spor na srđbu i pun dobrote. Zato ću dovijeka klicati milosrđu Božjemu.“** Slijedi zaključna molitva vječnom Bogu, „čije je milosrđe neistraživo i čije blago smilovanja neiscrpivo“. U njoj se moli da Bog umnoži milosrđe u vjernicima, „da u teškim trenucima ne očajavamo i ne budemo obeshrabreni“. Vjernici se trebaju predati „s velikim pouzdanjem“ Božjoj svetoj volji, „koja je sama ljubav i smilovanje“. Molitva se zaključuje po Isusu Kristu, **„kralju milosrđa“**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: uzdanje u Božje milosrđe, zazivanje Isusova imena i Marijin zagovor izražavaju kršćansku molitvu usmjerenu Bogu, a navedeni zazivi odgovaraju poznatoj pobožnosti Božjem milosrđu. Posebno je dobro što se pouzdanje povezuje s predanjem Božjoj volji, a ne s pretpostavkom da milosrđe uklanja potrebu za obraćenjem ili Božjim sudom.
magisterium.enrichment: Pobožnost Božjem milosrđu promatra Kristovu smrt i uskrsnuće kao izvor oproštenja i obnovljene radosti, pa njezine zazive valja razumjeti u svjetlu vazmenog otajstva i liturgije Crkve. Litanijski iskazi o krštenju, Crkvi, sakramentima i nadi očajnih sažimaju kako se Božje milosrđe očituje u spasenju i životu vjernika.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Catholic teaching: trust in God's mercy, invoking the name of Jesus, and Mary's intercession express Christian prayer directed to God, and the stated invocations correspond to the well-known devotion to Divine Mercy. It is particularly good that trust is connected with surrender to God's will, rather than with the assumption that mercy removes the need for conversion or God's judgment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Devotion to Divine Mercy views Christ's death and resurrection as the source of forgiveness and renewed joy, so its invocations should be understood in light of the paschal mystery and the liturgy of the Church. Litany statements about baptism, the Church, the sacraments, and the hope of the despairing summarize how God's mercy is manifested in salvation and the life of believers.

sections.subtitle_en: From „Holy God“ to the litany: thirty invocations to Divine Mercy
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays the Litany of Divine Mercy with the repeated response „I trust in you“
sections.content_en:
The Chaplet of Divine Mercy ends at 00:11:33 with the threefold invocation: **„Holy God, Holy Mighty One, Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us and on the whole world.“**

Then follow invocations of trust:

- „O Blood and Water, which gushed forth from the Heart of Jesus as a fount of mercy for us, I trust in you.“
- „Mary, Mother of Mercy, pray for us.“
- repeated three times **„Jesus, I trust in you.“**

### Litany of Divine Mercy

At 00:12:21 the Litany of Divine Mercy begins. After the usual introduction („Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy…“) and invocations to the Most Holy Trinity follows a long series of invocations. Each begins with the words „Divine Mercy“, and ends with the response **„I trust in you“**.

The invocations trace salvation history from creation to eternity. Mercy is described as:

- „incomprehensible mystery of the Most Holy Trinity“ and „expression of His greatest power“,
- that which was revealed „in the creation of heavenly spirits“ and which „called us from nothingness into life“,
- that which „protects us from deserved punishments“ and „frees us from the misery of sin“,
- that which „flows forth from the wounds of Christ“ and „gushes from the Sacred Heart“,
- that which „gave the Blessed Virgin as Mother of Mercy“,
- that visible in the establishment of the Church and sacraments, „unlimited in the sacrament of baptism and penance“ and „immense in the sacrament of the altar and priesthood“,
- „source for the sick and suffering“, „hope of those who despair“, and „peace of the dying“,
- that which „relieves the sufferings of souls in purgatory“ and which is „immense joy of all saints“,
- „inexhaustible source of miracles“.

### Concluding prayer

The litany concludes with the verse: **„God is merciful and full of compassion, slow to anger and full of goodness. Therefore forever I will sing the mercies of the Lord.“** Follows the concluding prayer to the eternal God, „whose mercy is unsearchable and whose treasure of compassion is inexhaustible“. In it, the prayer asks that God increase mercy in believers, „that in difficult moments we might not despair nor become discouraged“. Believers should submit „with great confidence“ to God's holy will, „which is love and compassion itself“. The prayer is concluded through Jesus Christ, **„King of Mercy“**.

sections.subtitle: Gospina krunica: uskrsnuće i uzašašće
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje prvo slavno otajstvo Gospine krunice, Isusovo uskrsnuće
sections.content:
U 00:16:40 voditelj najavljuje: **„Slijedi Gospina krunica.“** Moli se pet **slavnih otajstava**, koja prate Kristovu i Marijinu proslavu.

### Prvo otajstvo: „koji je od mrtvih uskrsnuo“

Prvo otajstvo posvećeno je Isusovu uskrsnuću. Kao i svaka desetica, počinje molitvom **Oče naš**, nakon koje slijedi deset **Zdravo Marija**. Ime Isusovo u svakoj Zdravo Mariji povezuje se s otajstvom koje se razmatra. Desetica završava molitvom **Slava Ocu** i zazivom:

> „O moj Isuse, oprosti nam naše grijehe. Očuvaj nas od paklenoga ognja. Dovedi u raj sve duše, osobito one kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe.“

Taj završni zaziv povezuje krunicu s temom epizode. I ovdje je u središtu milosrđe, i to prema dušama kojima je ono „najpotrebnije“.

### Drugo otajstvo: „koji je na nebo uzašao“

U 00:20:37 počinje drugo slavno otajstvo, Isusovo uzašašće na nebo. Desetica ima isti oblik: Oče naš, deset Zdravo Marija, Slava Ocu i ponovno molba da Isus oprosti grijehe, očuva od paklenoga ognja i dovede u raj sve duše. Voditelj desetice moli bez komentara, pa ponavljanje i tišina između molitava daju prostor za osobno razmatranje.

magisterium.assessment: Opis slavnih otajstava i njihove molitvene strukture u skladu je s katoličkom pobožnošću krunice: uskrsnuće i uzašašće Krista središnji su događaji vjere, a ponavljane molitve služe razmatranju tih otajstava. Zaziv za oproštenje i spasenje duša prikazan je kao molitvena prošnja za Božje milosrđe, ne como jamstvo da se svatko automatski spašava.
magisterium.enrichment: Uskrsnuće potvrđuje kršćansku vjeru i pobjedu života nad smrću, dok uzašašće označava Kristovo uzvišenje Ocu i njegovu slavu. Razmatranje tih otajstava u krunici ne odvraća od Krista: ono vjernika vodi dubljem promatranju njegova lica i nadi u konačno zajedništvo s Bogom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the glorious mysteries and their prayer structure is in accordance with the Catholic devotion of the Rosary: the resurrection and ascension of Christ are central events of faith, and repeated prayers serve meditation on these mysteries. The invocation for forgiveness and the salvation of souls is presented as a prayerful petition for God's mercy, not as a guarantee that everyone is automatically saved.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The resurrection confirms the Christian faith and the victory of life over death, while the ascension signifies Christ's exaltation to the Father and his glory. Meditation on these mysteries in the Rosary does not distract from Christ: it leads the believer to a deeper contemplation of his face and to hope in final communion with God.

sections.subtitle_en: The Rosary of Our Lady: resurrection and ascension
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the first glorious mystery of the Rosary of Our Lady, Jesus' resurrection
sections.content_en:
At 00:16:40 the host announces: **„Next is the Rosary of Our Lady.“** Five **glorious mysteries** are prayed, which follow Christ's and Mary's glorification.

### First mystery: „who rose from the dead“

The first mystery is dedicated to Jesus' resurrection. Like every decade, it begins with the **Our Father** prayer, followed by ten **Hail Marys**. The name of Jesus in each Hail Mary is linked to the mystery being contemplated. The decade ends with the **Glory Be to the Father** prayer and the invocation:

> „O my Jesus, forgive us our sins. Save us from the fires of hell. Lead all souls to heaven, especially those who are most in need of your mercy.“

That closing invocation links the rosary to the theme of the episode. Here too, mercy is at the center, specifically toward the souls that are „most in need“ of it.

### Second mystery: „who ascended into heaven“

At 00:20:37 the second glorious mystery begins, Jesus' ascension into heaven. The decade has the same form: Our Father, ten Hail Marys, Glory Be to the Father, and again the plea that Jesus forgive sins, save from the fires of hell, and lead all souls to heaven. The host prays the decades without commentary, so repetition and silence between prayers provide space for personal contemplation.

sections.subtitle: Duhovi, uznesenje i okrunjenje: vrhunac slavnih otajstava
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje peto slavno otajstvo, okrunjenje Blažene Djevice Marije
sections.content:
Druga polovica krunice prelazi s Kristove proslave na dar Duha Svetoga i Marijinu proslavu.

### Treće otajstvo: „koji je Duha Svetoga poslao“

U 00:24:37 voditelj najavljuje treće otajstvo, silazak Duha Svetoga. Nakon molitve Oče naš slijedi deset Zdravo Marija, zatim Slava Ocu i zaziv „O moj Isuse“. Molitva završava molbom za duše „kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe“.

### Četvrto otajstvo: „koji je tebe, Djevice, na nebo uznio“

U 00:28:30 počinje četvrto otajstvo, posvećeno uznesenju Blažene Djevice Marije na nebo. Desetica se moli istim redom i s istim zaključnim molbama za oproštenje, zaštitu od paklenoga ognja i spasenje svih duša.

### Peto otajstvo: „koji je tebe, Djevice, na nebu okrunio“

Zadnje otajstvo, najavljeno u 00:32:27, razmatra okrunjenje Marije na nebu. Time se zatvara slijed koji počinje Kristovim uskrsnućem, a završava proslavom njegove Majke.

Razmatranje Marijina okrunjenja pristaje Svetkovini Svih Svetih. Prvo stvorenje okrunjeno u nebeskoj slavi pokazuje cilj kojemu teže svi koji se nadaju „velikoj plaći na nebesima“ iz evanđelja dana.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkom vjerom: silazak Duha Svetoga, Marijino uznesenje i njezina nebeska proslava pripadaju kršćanskoj nadi i marijanskoj pobožnosti, a Marija u slavi pokazuje cilj svetosti kojemu je pozvana cijela Crkva. Ipak, tvrdnju da je Marija prvo stvorenje okrunjeno u nebeskoj slavi valja razumjeti kao pobožnu teološku formulaciju, ne kao zasebno definiranu dogmu niti kao izričit biblijski iskaz.
concerns: Krunica tradicionalno razmatra Marijino okrunjenje, ali taj se događaj ne opisuje izravno u Svetom pismu; zato ga treba predstaviti kao pobožno razmatranje, a ne kao biblijski izričitu činjenicu.
Izraz prvo stvorenje okrunjeno može zvučati preširoko ako se ne pojasni da se Marijina jedinstvena slava odnosi na njezino mjesto među otkupljenima i da je sva njezina slava usmjerena na Krista.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno razmatranje Marijina uznesenja naglašava da ono proslavlja Boga i Kristovu pobjedu nad grijehom i smrću te u Mariji pokazuje cilj svetosti kojemu je pozvano cijelo crkveno zajedništvo. Marija je jedinstvena među onima koji su izabrani i proslavljeni s Kristom, ali njezino zagovaranje i slava ne zamjenjuju Kristovo spasenjsko djelovanje, nego od njega ovise.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with the Catholic faith: the descent of the Holy Spirit, Mary's assumption, and her heavenly glorification belong to Christian hope and Marian devotion, and Mary in glory shows the goal of holiness to which the whole Church is called. Nevertheless, the claim that Mary is the first creature crowned in heavenly glory should be understood as a pious theological formulation, not as a separately defined dogma nor as an explicit biblical statement.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's contemplation of Mary's assumption emphasizes that it glorifies God and Christ's victory over sin and death, and in Mary shows the goal of holiness to which the entire ecclesial community is called. Mary is unique among those who are chosen and glorified with Christ, but her intercession and glory do not replace Christ's salvific action, but depend on it.
concerns_en: The Rosary traditionally contemplates Mary's coronation, but this event is not directly described in Sacred Scripture; therefore, it should be presented as a pious meditation, rather than as a biblically explicit fact.
The expression first creature crowned may sound overly broad if it is not clarified that Mary's unique glory refers to her place among the redeemed and that all her glory is directed toward Christ.

sections.subtitle_en: Pentecost, the Assumption, and the Coronation: climax of the glorious mysteries
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the fifth glorious mystery, the Coronation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
sections.content_en:
The second half of the rosary shifts from Christ's glorification to the gift of the Holy Spirit and Mary's glorification.

### Third mystery: „who sent the Holy Spirit“

At 00:24:37 the host announces the third mystery, the descent of the Holy Spirit. After the Our Father prayer follow ten Hail Marys, then Glory Be to the Father and the invocation „O my Jesus“. The prayer ends with a plea for souls „who are most in need of your mercy“.

### Fourth mystery: „who assumed you, Virgin, into heaven“

At 00:28:30 begins the fourth mystery, dedicated to the assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary into heaven. The decade is prayed in the same order and with the same concluding petitions for forgiveness, protection from the fire of hell, and salvation of all souls.

### Fifth mystery: „who crowned you, Virgin, in heaven“

The last mystery, announced at 00:32:27, contemplates the coronation of Mary in heaven. This closes the sequence that begins with Christ's resurrection and ends with the glorification of his Mother.

The contemplation of Mary's coronation suits the Solemnity of All Saints. The first creature crowned in heavenly glory shows the goal toward which all those strive who hope for the „great reward in heaven“ from the gospel of the day.

sections.subtitle: „Zdravo Kraljice“: molitva prognanih sinova Evinih
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli završnu marijansku molitvu „Zdravo Kraljice“
sections.content:
Molitveni dio završava u 00:36:26 molitvom **„Zdravo Kraljice“**. Mariju se u njoj pozdravlja kao „majku milosrđa, život, slast i ufanje naše“. Naziv „majka milosrđa“ veže ovu molitvu uz glavnu temu emisije, kao i ranije zazive Mariji u Krunici Božjeg milosrđa.

Molitva opisuje ljudski život kao progonstvo: **„K tebi vapijemo, prognani sinovi Evini, k tebi uzdišemo tugujući i plačući u ovoj suznoj dolini.“** Mariju se zatim moli kao „zagovornicu“ da svrne „one svoje milostive oči na nas“ i da „poslije ovoga progona“ pokaže Isusa, „blagoslovljeni plod utrobe svoje“.

Molitva završava trostrukim zazivom: **„O blaga, o mila, o slatka Djevice Marijo.“** Zemaljski život prikazan je kao suzna dolina, a nada je usmjerena prema susretu s Kristom u vječnosti, isto kao u evanđelju dana koje obećava nagradu na nebesima.

Posljednjim „Amen“ zatvara se gotovo trideset sedam minuta neprekinute molitve. Voditelj odmah najavljuje sljedeći dio emisije: **„Slijedi tumačenje svete riječi“**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je jasno usklađen s katoličkom molitvenom tradicijom: Mariju naziva majkom i zagovornicom, a završna nada usmjerena je prema Isusu, plodu njezine utrobe. Slika zemaljskog života kao suzne doline izražava kušnje i čežnju za nebeskim ispunjenjem, a ne poricanje dobrote stvorenoga svijeta.
magisterium.enrichment: Molitva Zdravo Kraljice sama povezuje vapaj prognane djece Evine s molbom Mariji da nam nakon ovoga progonstva pokaže Isusa, pa je njezino središte konačno Krist. Katoličko razumijevanje Marijina zagovora vidi ga kao majčinsko posredovanje koje nas upućuje njezinu Sinu; Crkva ga ne poistovjećuje s Kristovim jedinstvenim posredništvom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is clearly aligned with the Catholic prayer tradition: it calls Mary mother and advocate, and final hope is directed toward Jesus, the fruit of her womb. The image of earthly life as a valley of tears expresses trials and longing for heavenly fulfillment, rather than a denial of the goodness of the created world.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The prayer Hail, Holy Queen itself connects the cry of the exiled children of Eve with the petition to Mary to show us Jesus after this exile, so its center is ultimately Christ. The Catholic understanding of Mary's intercession sees it as a maternal mediation that directs us to her Son; the Church does not equate it with Christ's unique mediation.

sections.subtitle_en: „Hail, Holy Queen“: prayer of the banished children of Eve
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recites the concluding Marian prayer „Hail, Holy Queen“
sections.content_en:
The prayer section ends at 00:36:26 with the prayer **„Hail, Holy Queen“**. In it Mary is greeted as „Mother of Mercy, our life, our sweetness, and our hope“. The title „Mother of Mercy“ links this prayer to the main theme of the program, as well as to earlier invocations to Mary in the Chaplet of Divine Mercy.

The prayer describes human life as an exile: **„To you do we cry, poor banished children of Eve; to you do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.“** Mary is then implored as „advocate“ to turn „your eyes of mercy toward us“ and „after this exile“ show Jesus, „the blessed fruit of your womb“.

The prayer concludes with the threefold invocation: **„O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.“** Earthly life is depicted as a valley of tears, and hope is directed toward an encounter with Christ in eternity, just as in the gospel of the day which promises a reward in heaven.

With the final „Amen“, nearly thirty-seven minutes of uninterrupted prayer comes to an end. The host immediately announces the next part of the program: **„Next is the interpretation of the holy word“**.

sections.subtitle: Patmoska vizija: opečaćeni i nebrojeno mnoštvo u bijelim haljinama
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Vladimir Grebenar započinje čitanje iz Knjige Otkrivenja nakon završene molitve Zdravo Kraljice
sections.content:
Nakon krunice Božjega milosrđa, Gospine krunice i molitve *Zdravo Kraljice*, voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** prelazi na središnji dio emisije, tumačenje svete riječi za svetkovinu Svih svetih. Prvo čitanje uzeto je iz Knjige Otkrivenja i donosi jednu od najsnažnijih slika posljednje knjige Biblije.

U čitanju apostol Ivan opisuje kako vidi „drugog jednog anđela“ koji uzlazi od istoka sunčeva s pečatom Boga živoga. Taj anđeo iza glasa doviknuje četvorici anđela kojima je dano nauditi zemlji i moru: „Ne udite ni zemlji ni moru ni drveću dok ne opečatimo sluge Boga našega na čelima.“ Zatim se navodi broj opečaćenih, **144.000 iz svih plemena sinova Izraelovih**.

Vizija se potom širi. Ivan vidi veliko mnoštvo koje nitko ne može izbrojiti, iz svakog naroda, plemena, puka i jezika. Stoje pred prijestoljem i pred Jaganjcem, odjeveni u bijele haljine, s palmama u rukama, i kliču: „Spasenje Bogu našemu koji sjedi na prijestolju i Jaganjcu.“ Svi anđeli oko prijestolja, starješine i četiri bića padaju ničice i klanjaju se Bogu, pjevajući o blagoslovu, slavi, mudrosti, zahvalnici, časti, moći i snazi Bogu u vijeke vjekova.

Čitanje završava dijalogom koji daje ključ cijelog odlomka. Jedan od starješina pita tko su ti odjeveni u bijelo i odakle dolaze. Ivan odgovara: „Gospodine moj, ti to znaš.“ Starješina tada otkriva: „Oni dođoše iz nevolje velike i oprali su haljine svoje i ubijelili ih u krvi Jaganjčevoj.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak vjerno prenosi Otkrivenje 7, uključujući pečaćenje Božjih slugu, hvalu Bogu i Jaganjcu te bijele haljine oprane u Jaganjčevoj krvi. Prikaz je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem spasenja po Kristu i ne nameće spornu doslovnu interpretaciju broja 144.000.
magisterium.enrichment: Broj 144.000 tumači se simbolički: upućuje na puninu Božjeg naroda, a vizija velikog mnoštva iz svih naroda naglašava univerzalni poziv na spasenje. Bijele haljine označuju očišćenje Kristovom smrću i milošću, kojem se vjernici pridružuju krštenjem, pokorom i vjernim svjedočenjem; velika nevolja ne mora označavati samo mučeništvo.

The portrayal is in accordance with the Catholic understanding of salvation through Christ and does not impose a disputed literal interpretation of the number 144,000.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The number 144,000 is interpreted symbolically: it points to the fullness of the people of God, and the vision of a great multitude from all nations emphasizes the universal call to salvation. White robes signify purification by Christ's death and grace, which believers join through baptism, penance, and faithful witness; the great tribulation need not designate martyrdom alone.

sections.subtitle_en: Patmos vision: the sealed and a countless multitude in white robes
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Vladimir Grebenar begins reading from the Book of Revelation after concluding the Hail, Holy Queen prayer
sections.content_en:
After the Chaplet of Divine Mercy, the Rosary of Our Lady, and the prayer *Hail, Holy Queen*, host **Vladimir Grebenar** moves to the central part of the broadcast, the interpretation of the holy word for the solemnity of All Saints. The first reading is taken from the Book of Revelation and brings one of the most powerful images of the final book of the Bible.

In the reading, the apostle John describes how he sees „another angel“ ascending from the rising of the sun with the seal of the living God. That angel calls out with a loud voice to the four angels who were given power to harm the earth and the sea: „Do not harm the earth or the sea or the trees until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.“ Then the number of those sealed is given, **144,000 from all the tribes of the children of Israel**.

The vision then widens. John sees a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people, and tongue. They stand before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and cry out: „Salvation belongs to our God who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.“ All the angels around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures fall on their faces and worship God, singing of blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might to God forever and ever.

The reading concludes with a dialogue that provides the key to the entire passage. One of the elders asks who these clothed in white are and where they come from. John replies: „My lord, you know.“ The elder then reveals: „These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.“

sections.subtitle: Anđeo s istoka: sud koji vjernima donosi oslobođenje, a grešnima osudu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar objašnjava da anđeo koji dolazi s istoka simbolizira Božji sud
sections.content:
Tumačenje Vladimir Grebenar započinje kontekstom. Riječ je o viđenju koje je sveti Ivan apostol imao na otoku **Patmosu**, kada je od Isusa dobio zadaću zapisati posljednju knjigu koja će ući u kanon, posljednju knjigu Biblije.

Zatim se zadržava na jednom detalju: anđeo dolazi **s istoka sunčeva**. „S istoka tko dolazi? Sud“, kaže voditelj. Da je riječ o sudu, prema njegovu tumačenju potvrđuje i to što anđeo nosi pečat Boga živoga.

Taj sud, objašnjava Grebenar, ima dvostruko lice:

- **za vjerne** on znači oslobođenje od tereta, zbog čega anđeo pečati upravo njih;
- **za grešne** isti taj sud postaje osuda.

Voditelj to opisuje kao **„veliki preokret“**. Oni koji su prošli kroz veliku nevolju i ubijelili haljine u krvi Jaganjčevoj nosili su, kako kaže, velike pritiske, terete, umor i „žegu dana“ te podnosili tegobe za kraljevstvo Božje. Kada dođe sud s istoka, Bog se proslavi, njih oslobodi, a osudi one koji su činili zlo i nisu se obratili.

Iz toga izvodi poruku za slušatelje: postoji vrijeme dano za obraćenje, a nakon njega „nema više“, to je vrijeme prošlo. „Ovo je opomena za nas“, zaključuje.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na obraćenje i tvrdnja da Božji sud očituje i spasenje vjernih i osudu zla mogu se uskladiti s kršćanskom vjerom, ali tumačenje da „s istoka” znači sud nije potkrijepljeno navedenim biblijskim odlomkom niti dostupnim katoličkim komentarima. Odlomak također može stvoriti dojam da pečat po sebi oslobađa vjerne od zemaljskih kušnji, premda vizija govori o mnoštvu koje je prošlo kroz veliku nevolju.
concerns: Simboliku anđela koji dolazi s istoka sunčeva kao znak suda iznosi kao određeno tumačenje, ali Otkrivenje 7 u dostavljenim izvorima ne utvrđuje takvo značenje.
Pečaćenje slugu Boga živoga ne bi trebalo tumačiti kao obećanje da vjernici neće trpjeti ili biti izloženi nevoljama; tekst istodobno opisuje spašene kao one koji su prošli kroz veliku nevolju.

Formulacija da nakon određenog vremena za obraćenje „nema više” zvuči kao neposredna tvrdnja o kraju mogućnosti obraćenja, a ne kao općenita opomena o konačnom sudu; treba je izreći precizno i bez neutemeljenog određivanja vremena.
magisterium.enrichment: U samom odlomku anđeo s pečatom zaustavlja štetu dok se Božji sluge ne označe, a odmah zatim slijedi vizija mnoštva spašenih iz svih naroda; tekst sam po sebi ne poistovjećuje pečat nipošto s izuzećem od svih kušnji. Bijele haljine biblijski su povezane s očišćenjem u krvi Jaganjčevoj, odnosno sa spasenjem koje dolazi po Kristu, a ne s vlastitom bezgrešnošću ili povlasticom neovisnom o njemu. Zato se poziv na obraćenje može zadržati, uz izbjegavanje neprovjerene tvrdnje o istoku kao znaku suda i pretjerano kategorične vremenske opomene.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to conversion and the claim that God's judgment manifests both the salvation of the faithful and the condemnation of evil can be reconciled with Christian faith, but the interpretation that "from the east" means judgment is not supported by the cited biblical passage or available Catholic commentaries. The passage can also create the impression that the seal in itself frees the faithful from earthly trials, even though the vision speaks of a multitude that has passed through the great tribulation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In the passage itself, the angel with the seal halts harm until the servants of God are marked, and immediately following is the vision of the multitude of the saved from all nations; the text in itself by no means equates the seal with exemption from all trials. White robes are biblically connected with purification in the blood of the Lamb, that is, with the salvation that comes through Christ, rather than with one's own sinlessness or a privilege independent of him. Therefore, the call to conversion can be maintained, while avoiding the unverified claim about the east as a sign of judgment and an overly categorical temporal warning.
concerns_en: The symbolism of the angel coming from the rising of the sun as a sign of judgment is presented as a definite interpretation, but Revelation 7 in the provided sources does not establish such a meaning.

The sealing of the servants of the living God should not be interpreted as a promise that believers will not suffer or be exposed to tribulations; the text simultaneously describes the saved as those who have passed through the great tribulation.

The phrasing that after a certain time for conversion "there is no more" sounds like an immediate claim about the end of the possibility of conversion, rather than a general warning about the final judgment; it should be stated precisely and without unjustified determination of time.

sections.subtitle_en: The angel from the east: judgment bringing deliverance to the faithful and condemnation to sinners
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar explains that the angel coming from the east symbolizes God's judgment
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar begins the interpretation with context. It concerns a vision that Saint John the Apostle had on the island of **Patmos**, when he received the task from Jesus to write down the final book that would enter the canon, the final book of the Bible.

Then he lingers on one detail: the angel comes **from the rising of the sun**. „From the east, who comes? Judgment“, says the host. That it is a matter of judgment, according to his interpretation, is also confirmed by the fact that the angel bears the seal of the living God.

That judgment, Grebenar explains, has a two-fold face:

- **for the faithful** it means deliverance from burdens, which is why the angel seals precisely them;
- **for sinners** that same judgment becomes condemnation.

The host describes this as a **„great turning point“**. Those who passed through the great tribulation and made their robes white in the blood of the Lamb bore, as he says, great pressures, burdens, fatigue, and the „heat of the day“, and endured hardships for the kingdom of God. When judgment comes from the east, God is glorified, delivers them, and condemns those who did evil and did not convert.

From this he draws a message for the listeners: there is a time given for conversion, and after it „there is no more“, that time has passed. „This is a warning for us“, he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Četiri anđela na četiri strane svijeta i Sotona koji „rešeta“ Crkvu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori kako đavao ne može ništa učiniti dok mu Bog Otac ne da vlast
sections.content:
Sljedeći dio tumačenja posvećen je četvorici anđela kojima se obraća anđeo s pečatom Boga živoga. Vladimir Grebenar objašnjava da oni stoje na četiri strane svijeta, **istoku, zapadu, sjeveru i jugu**, te da svaka od tih strana ima svoje značenje.

Prenoseći sliku u svakodnevni život, voditelj kaže da ti anđeli na neki način drže ravnotežu, odnosno da drže stvari **pod Božjom kontrolom**. Iz toga izvodi jedno od ključnih teoloških polazišta svoga tumačenja: „Đavao ne može činiti ništa dok mu Bog Otac ne da vlast.“ Prema njegovim riječima, đavao ne može zagospodariti svijetom ni na određeno vrijeme ako mu Bog Otac to ne dopusti.

Kao biblijsku potvrdu navodi Isusove riječi upućene Petru: „Sotona je dobio vlast da vas prorešeta kao pšenicu.“ Grebenar tumači da Sotona može dobiti vlast da napadne i udari Crkvu, ali sa svrhom **pročišćenja**. Oni koji nisu Kristovi time otpadaju, a oni koji jesu Kristovi izbjeljuju svoje haljine u krvi Jaganjčevoj, „u muci velikoj“. Time zatvara krug s prvim čitanjem: velika nevolja iz Otkrivenja za njega je upravo to rešetanje kroz koje vjernici prolaze.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje je djelomično usklađeno: Otkrivenje doista prikazuje anđele koji zadržavaju štetne sile dok se Božji sluge ne označe pečatom, a mnoštvo dolazi iz velike nevolje i pere haljine u krvi Jaganjčevoj. Ipak, tumač iznosi nekoliko interpretacija kao da su izravno utvrđene u tekstu, osobito poistovjećivanje velike nevolje sa „rešetanjem“ Crkve i tvrdnju da oni koji nisu Kristovi tada otpadaju.
concerns: Otkrivenje govori o četiri anđela na „četiri ugla zemlje“ i o četiri vjetra; ne navodi izričito istok, zapad, sjever i jug niti posebna značenja koja pripadaju svakoj strani. Takvo simboličko tumačenje može biti dopušteno, ali treba ga označiti kao tumačenje, a ne kao izričit sadržaj teksta.

Luka 22,31 ne kaže da je Sotona „dobio vlast“, nego da je „zaiskao“ da učenike rešeta poput pšenice. To podupire misao da je zlo pod Božjim dopuštenjem ograničeno, ali je preciznije reći da Bog zlo dopušta nego tvrditi da Sotoni daje vlast, što može zvučati kao neposredno odobravanje njegova djelovanja.

Luka govori o kušnji učenika, Petrovu mogućem padu i Isusovoj molitvi za njegovu vjeru; ne poistovjećuje tu epizodu s velikom nevoljom iz Otkrivenja. Povezivanje tih prizora može biti duhovna analogija, ali nije dokaz da je velika nevolja upravo Sotonino rešetanje Crkve.

Otkrivenje kaže da su oni u bijelim haljinama prošli kroz veliku nevolju i da su oprali haljine u krvi Jaganjčevoj, ali ne kaže da svi oni koji nisu Kristovi nužno otpadaju niti da svaka kušnja sama po sebi pročišćuje vjernika. Tekst naglašava spasenje po Jaganjcu, a ne jednostavnu podjelu prema kojoj kušnja automatski otkriva tko je Kristov.
magisterium.enrichment: Slika pečata i anđela u Otkrivenju naglašava da Božji sluge pripadaju Bogu i da razorne sile ne djeluju izvan granica Božje vlasti; sam tekst najprije nalaže da se sluge zapečate, a zatim prikazuje mnoštvo koje štuje Jaganjca. „Oprati haljine u krvi Jaganjčevoj“ paradoksalna je slika očišćenja koje dolazi po Kristovoj smrti i milosti, a ne po samoj patnji.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation is partially aligned: Revelation indeed depicts angels restraining harmful forces until the servants of God are marked with a seal, and a multitude comes out of the great tribulation and washes their robes in the blood of the Lamb. Nevertheless, the interpreter puts forward several interpretations as if they were directly established in the text, especially the identification of the great tribulation with the "sifting" of the Church and the claim that those who are not Christ's fall away at that time.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The imagery of the seal and angels in Revelation emphasizes that the servants of God belong to God and that destructive forces do not act outside the limits of God's authority; the text itself first commands that the servants be sealed, and then depicts the multitude worshipping the Lamb. "To wash robes in the blood of the Lamb" is a paradoxical image of purification that comes through Christ's death and grace, and not through suffering alone.
concerns_en: Revelation speaks of four angels at the "four corners of the earth" and of four winds; it does not explicitly state east, west, north, and south, nor special meanings belonging to each direction. Such symbolic interpretation may be permissible, but it should be marked as an interpretation, and not as explicit content of the text.

Luke 22:31 does not say that Satan "received authority," but that he "demanded" to sift the disciples like wheat. This supports the thought that evil is limited under God's permission, but it is more precise to say that God permits evil than to claim that he gives authority to Satan, which can sound like immediate approval of his action.

Luke speaks of the testing of the disciples, Peter's possible fall, and Jesus' prayer for his faith; he does not equate that episode with the great tribulation from Revelation. Connecting these scenes may be a spiritual analogy, but it is not proof that the great tribulation is precisely Satan's sifting of the Church.

Revelation says that those in white robes passed through the great tribulation and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb, but it does not say that all who are not Christ's necessarily fall away nor that every trial in itself purifies the believer. The text emphasizes salvation through the Lamb, rather than a simple division according to which a trial automatically reveals who belongs to Christ.

sections.subtitle_en: Four angels at the four corners of the earth and Satan „sifting“ the Church
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about how the devil cannot do anything until God the Father gives him authority
sections.content_en:
The next part of the interpretation is dedicated to the four angels addressed by the angel with the seal of the living God. Vladimir Grebenar explains that they stand at the four corners of the earth, **east, west, north, and south**, and that each of those directions has its meaning.

Translating the image into everyday life, the host says that those angels in some way maintain balance, that is, they keep things **under God's control**. From this he draws one of the key theological starting points of his interpretation: „The devil can do nothing until God the Father gives him authority.“ According to his words, the devil cannot take control of the world even for a specific time if God the Father does not permit it to him.

As biblical confirmation he cites Jesus' words addressed to Peter: „Satan has obtained permission to sift you like wheat.“ Grebenar interprets that Satan can receive authority to attack and strike the Church, but for the purpose of **purification**. Those who are not Christ's thereby fall away, and those who are Christ's whiten their robes in the blood of the Lamb, „in great suffering“. He thus closes the circle with the first reading: the great tribulation from Revelation is for him precisely this sifting through which believers pass.

sections.subtitle: Viđenje nakon mise: četiri anđela prije nego što je poznavao čitanje
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar pripovijeda kako je u molitvi nakon svete mise vidio četiri anđela
sections.content:
Tumačenje zatim dobiva osobnu notu. Vladimir Grebenar priznaje da mu je ovo čitanje **„vrlo znakovito“** i objašnjava zašto. Emisiju, kaže, snima 31. listopada, a toga je jutra, prije nego što je pripremio tekst za sutrašnju svetkovinu, bio na svetoj misi.

Nakon što je primio tijelo Kristovo, ostao je u molitvi i nakon mise, uzeo si vremena i ušao „malo dublje u molitvu“. Tada je, prema vlastitom svjedočanstvu, imao iskustvo koje ga je iznenadilo: „Znate što sam vidio? Vidio sam **četiri anđela**. Nisam znao da je to današnje čitanje.“

Na tom mjestu stane i najavi da je vidio još nešto. Prije nego što to otkrije, prelazi na psalam za ovu svetkovinu.

magisterium.assessment: Opis osobnog viđenja četiriju anđela sam po sebi ne proturječi katoličkom nauku, ali iz samog svjedočanstva nije moguće zaključiti da je iskustvo nadnaravnog podrijetla niti da ono potvrđuje određeno tumačenje čitanja. Katolička vjera razlikuje takva moguća privatna iskustva od javne Objave i traži da ih se razborito prosuđuje u skladu s vjerom Crkve.
concerns: Iznenađenje zbog podudarnosti s liturgijskim čitanjem nije samo po sebi dokaz božanskog podrijetla viđenja; odlomak zasad ne tvrdi izričito da takav dokaz postoji, pa je važno ostati suzdržan u zaključivanju.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk uči da privatne objave ne nadopunjuju ni ne ispravljaju konačnu Kristovu Objavu, nego mogu, ako su autentične, pomoći vjernicima da je potpunije žive. Zato se osobno iskustvo može pripovijedati kao svjedočanstvo, ali ne treba ga izjednačiti sa Svetim pismom ili predstaviti kao obvezujuću poruku za druge vjernike.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of a personal vision of four angels in itself does not contradict Catholic teaching, but from the testimony itself it is not possible to conclude that the experience is of supernatural origin or that it confirms a specific interpretation of the readings. The Catholic faith distinguishes such possible private experiences from public Revelation and requires that they be prudently judged in accordance with the faith of the Church.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic doctrine teaches that private revelations neither complete nor correct the definitive Revelation of Christ, but can, if authentic, help believers to live it more fully. Therefore, personal experience can be narrated as a testimony, but it should not be equated with Sacred Scripture or presented as a binding message for other believers.
concerns_en: Surprise at the coincidence with the liturgical reading is not in itself proof of the divine origin of the vision; the passage so far does not explicitly claim that such proof exists, so it is important to remain restrained in drawing conclusions.

sections.subtitle_en: A vision after Mass: four angels before he knew the reading
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar recounts how in prayer after Holy Mass he saw four angels
sections.content_en:
The interpretation then takes on a personal note. Vladimir Grebenar admits that this reading is **„very meaningful“** to him and explains why. He says he is recording the program on October 31, and that morning, before preparing the text for tomorrow's solemnity, he was at Holy Mass.

After receiving the body of Christ, he remained in prayer after Mass as well, took some time, and went „a little deeper into prayer“. Then, according to his own testimony, he had an experience that surprised him: „You know what I saw? I saw **four angels**. I didn't know that was today's reading.“

At that point he pauses and announces that he saw something else. Before revealing it, he moves on to the psalm for this solemnity.

sections.subtitle: „Gospodnja je zemlja i sve na njoj“: tko će uzići na goru Gospodnju
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj čita psalam o čistom srcu i nedužnim rukama
sections.content:
Psalam koji Vladimir Grebenar čita naglašava Božje vlasništvo nad svim stvorenim: „Gospodnja je zemlja i sve na njoj, svijet i svi koji na njemu žive. On ga na morima utemelji i na rijekama učvrsti.“

Zatim slijede retorička pitanja: „Tko će uzići na goru Gospodnju? Tko će stajati na svetom mjestu njegovu?“ Odgovor psalma glasi da je to **onaj u koga su ruke nedužne i srce čisto**, čija se duša ne predaje ispraznosti. Takav prima blagoslov od Gospodina i nagradu od Boga, spasitelja svoga. Psalam završava riječima: „Takav je naraštaj onih koji traže njega, koji traže lice Boga Jakovljeva.“

U kontekstu svetkovine Svih svetih psalam ocrtava upravo onu skupinu o kojoj govori Otkrivenje, ljude čista srca koji traže Božje lice.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje je u skladu s Ps 24: psalam povezuje pripadnost svega stvorenoga Gospodinu s pozivom na čistoću djelovanja i srca te traženje Božjeg lica. Poveznica sa svetkovinom Svih svetih prikladna je kao duhovno čitanje, premda je bolje shvatiti je kao tematsku primjenu nego kao tvrdnju da psalam izravno opisuje određenu skupinu iz Otkrivenja.
magisterium.enrichment: „Čiste ruke i čisto srce” obuhvaćaju i djela i nutarnje nakane, a ne samo vanjsku neporočnost. Kršćanska svetost nije tek ljudsko postignuće: Bog čovjeka čisti i privodi svojoj prisutnosti, dok ga psalam poziva da odgovori životom koji traži Gospodina.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation is in accordance with Ps 24: the psalm connects the belonging of all creation to the Lord with the call to purity of action and heart and seeking the face of God. The link with the Solemnity of All Saints is appropriate as a spiritual reading, although it is better understood as a thematic application rather than a claim that the psalm directly describes a specific group from Revelation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: "Clean hands and a pure heart" encompass both deeds and interior intentions, and not merely external blamelessness. Christian holiness is not a mere human achievement: God cleanses man and brings him into His presence, while the psalm invites him to respond with a life that seeks the Lord.

sections.subtitle_en: „The earth is the Lord's and all that is in it“: who shall ascend the hill of the Lord
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reads a psalm about a clean heart and innocent hands
sections.content_en:
The psalm that Vladimir Grebenar reads emphasizes God's ownership over all creation: „The earth is the Lord's and all that is in it, the world and all who live in it. For he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.“

Then follow rhetorical questions: „Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord? Who shall stand in his holy place?“ The psalm's answer is that it is **the one whose hands are innocent and whose heart is pure**, whose soul does not surrender to vanity. Such a one receives a blessing from the Lord and a reward from God, his savior. The psalm concludes with the words: „Such is the generation of those who seek him, who seek the face of the God of Jacob.“

In the context of the solemnity of All Saints, the psalm outlines precisely that group spoken of in Revelation, people of pure heart who seek God's face.

magisterium.assessment: Samo pripovijedanje o viđenju i povezivanje s događajima nisu sami po sebi protivni katoličkom nauku, ali riječ je o privatnoj objavi čiji se sadržaj ne može izjednačiti sa Svetim pismom niti se od vjernika traži da ga prihvate kao vjeru. Budući da nije navedeno na koje se biblijsko mjesto upućuje, a predviđanja nemira iznesena su bez vidljivog razlučivanja, od slušatelja se traži oprezan, a ne lakovjeran pristup.
concerns: Poziv „kako stoji pisano u Svetom pismu” ostaje neodređen; bez konkretnog odlomka nije moguće prosuditi tumači li se tekst vjerno ili se biblijskom autoritetu pridružuje privatno viđenje.

Povezivanje viđenja s aktualnim prosvjedima i tvrdnja da će se nemiri širiti mogu ostaviti dojam potvrđenog proročanstva. Privatne objave ne nadopunjuju Kristovu konačnu objavu, nisu obvezujuće za vjernike i valja ih prosuđivati razborito; samo izneseni sadržaj ne utvrđuje da je viđenje autentično ni da su najavljeni događaji Božja poruka.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno učenje razlikuje javnu objavu, kojoj pripadaju Sveto pismo i apostolska predaja, od privatnih objava: potonje mogu pomoći živjeti evanđelje u određenom vremenu, ali ne mogu ga zamijeniti niti ga dovršiti. Njihovo mjerilo jest usmjerenost Kristu i sukladnost vjeri i ćudoređu; vjernik im može pristupiti razborito, ali nije dužan prihvatiti ih.

magisterium.assessment_en: The mere narration of the vision and connection with events are not in themselves contrary to Catholic teaching, but it is a matter of private revelation whose content cannot be equated with Sacred Scripture nor are believers required to accept it as faith. Since it is not specified which biblical passage is referenced, and predictions of unrest are presented without visible discernment, a cautious rather than credulous approach is required from listeners.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching distinguishes public revelation, to which Sacred Scripture and apostolic tradition belong, from private revelations: the latter can help live the gospel at a specific time, but cannot replace or complete it. Their criterion is Christ-centeredness and conformity with faith and morals; a believer may approach them prudently, but is not obliged to accept them.
concerns_en: The invocation "as it is written in Sacred Scripture" remains indeterminate; without a specific passage, it is impossible to judge whether the text is faithfully interpreted or whether a private vision is attached to biblical authority.

Connecting the vision with current protests and the claim that unrest will spread can leave the impression of a confirmed prophecy. Private revelations do not complete Christ's definitive revelation, are not binding on believers, and must be judged prudently; the presented content alone does not establish that the vision is authentic or that the announced events are God's message.
