sections.subtitle: Gospine poruke bez odjeka i poziv hrvatskom narodu na „Božji ustanak“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva hrvatski narod na Božji ustanak kroz post, molitvu i pokoru
sections.content:
Kao jedini način na koji se nemiri mogu spriječiti Vladimir Grebenar navodi ono na što poziva Gospa. U posljednjoj poruci, podsjeća, Gospa je pozvala da se **pojača molitva**.

Voditelj ne skriva razočaranje: „Žalostan sam što se Gospine poruke odbacuju.“ Poruke se, kaže, objavljuju po društvenim mrežama, ali ih „nitko ne doživljava“. Vrlo malo ljudi posti i moli na pravi način, a narod se premalo poziva na ustrajnost u molitvi i postu. „Jako, jako slabo, braćo i sestre, za zlo koje je u svijetu“, ocjenjuje.

Prema njegovoj procjeni, prosječna duhovnost u zapadnoj Europi i zapadnom svijetu preslaba je da bi se oduprla Sotoninoj moći. Za to su, kaže, potrebni **jaki postovi, ustrajne molitve i činjenje za Gospodina**.

Potom iznosi i težu ocjenu: zlo se u svijetu, smatra, više ni ne može spriječiti, jer je Sotona „zauzeo pozicije za veliku bitku i pripada mu što mu pripada“. Ipak, vidi iznimku. Zlo se, prema njegovim riječima, može spriječiti tamo gdje živi hrvatski narod i gdje ima vjere. Zato upućuje izravan poziv:

> Hrvatski narod mora se podići na ustanak, ali Božju bitku, Božji ustanak: post, molitva, pokora i činjenje za Gospodina.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na molitvu, post, pokoru i djelovanje za Gospodina u skladu je s katoličkom duhovnom tradicijom, a zlo i napastovanje Sotone stvarne su teme kršćanskog nauka. Ipak, tvrdnje da se zlo više ne može spriječiti u svijetu te da je hrvatski narod iznimka teološki su neprimjereno fatalističke i nacionalno isključive; izraz „Božji ustanak” prihvatljiv je samo ako je nedvosmisleno riječ o nenasilnoj duhovnoj borbi.
concerns: Privatne objave, pa i one pripisane Gospi, ne mogu se postaviti kao jedini put za sprečavanje nemira niti kao obvezujući temelj katoličke vjere. Crkva ih prosuđuje prema sukladnosti s jedinom javnom Objavom dovršenom u Kristu.

Tvrdnja da se zlo više ne može spriječiti može sugerirati da je Sotonina moć konačna ili da je Kristovo spasenjsko djelovanje osujećeno. Katolički nauk priznaje ozbiljan utjecaj Zloga, ali ne poriče ljudsku slobodu, odgovornost ni djelotvornost Kristova spasenja.

Nema osnove da se mogućnost sprečavanja zla na poseban način pripiše hrvatskom narodu ili području na kojem on živi; takvo izdvajanje može zvučati kao nacionalna povlaštenost. „Ustanak” treba izričito razumjeti kao duhovni poziv na obraćenje i dobra djela, a ne kao politički ili nasilni poziv.
magisterium.enrichment: Molitva, post i pokora mogu biti stvarni oblici obraćenja i suradnje vjernika s Božjim djelovanjem; crkveni izvori ih povezuju s Evanđeljem i odgovornim življenjem vjere, a ne s jamstvom da će određena skupina ljudi zaustaviti zlo. Kršćanski odgovor na zlo zato uključuje ustrajnost, odbacivanje grijeha i pouzdanje u Krista, bez tvrdnje da je konačni ishod već izgubljen.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to prayer, fasting, penance, and action for the Lord is in accordance with the Catholic spiritual tradition, and evil and temptation by Satan are real themes of Christian teaching. However, claims that evil can no longer be prevented in the world and that the Croatian people are an exception are theologically inappropriately fatalistic and nationally exclusive; the expression "God's uprising" is acceptable only if it is unmistakably a matter of nonviolent spiritual struggle.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Prayer, fasting, and penance can be genuine forms of conversion and cooperation of believers with God's action; church sources link them with the Gospel and responsible living of faith, and not with a guarantee that a specific group of people will halt evil. The Christian response to evil therefore includes perseverance, rejection of sin, and trust in Christ, without claiming that the final outcome is already lost.
concerns_en: Private revelations, even those attributed to Our Lady, cannot be posited as the sole way to prevent unrest or as a binding foundation of Catholic faith. The Church judges them according to conformity with the sole public Revelation completed in Christ.

The claim that evil can no longer be prevented may suggest that Satan's power is definitive or that Christ's salvific action is thwarted. Catholic teaching acknowledges the serious influence of the Evil One, but does not deny human freedom, responsibility, or the efficacy of Christ's salvation.

There is no basis for attributing the ability to prevent evil in a special way to the Croatian people or the territory in which they live; such singling out can sound like national privilege. "Uprising" must be explicitly understood as a spiritual call to conversion and good works, and not as a political or violent call.

sections.subtitle_en: Our Lady's messages without resonance and a call to the Croatian people for a „God's uprising“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host calls the Croatian people to God's uprising through fasting, prayer, and penance
sections.content_en:
As the only way in which the unrest can be prevented, Vladimir Grebenar mentions what Our Lady calls for. In the latest message, he recalls, Our Lady called for prayer to be **intensified**.

The host does not hide his disappointment: „I am sorrowful that Our Lady's messages are being rejected.“ The messages, he says, are published across social networks, but „no one pays attention to them“. Very few people fast and pray the right way, and people are too seldom called to perseverance in prayer and fasting. „Very, very poor, brothers and sisters, for the evil that is in the world“, he assesses.

According to his assessment, average spirituality in Western Europe and the Western world is too weak to resist Satan's power. For that, he says, **strong fasts, persistent prayers, and doing for the Lord** are needed.

Then he presents an even harsher assessment: evil in the world, he believes, can no longer even be prevented, because Satan has „taken positions for the great battle and what belongs to him belongs to him“. Yet he sees an exception. Evil can, according to his words, be prevented where the Croatian people live and where there is faith. Therefore he issues a direct call:

> The Croatian people must rise up in an uprising, but God's battle, God's uprising: fasting, prayer, penance, and doing for the Lord.

sections.subtitle: „Djeca se Božja zovemo i jesmo“: uzbuđenje pred neizvjesnom vječnošću
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar s radošću govori o vječnosti koju je Bog pripremio
sections.content:
Drugo čitanje uzeto je iz **Prve Ivanove poslanice**: „Predragi, gledajte koliku nam je ljubav darovao Otac: djeca se Božja zovemo i jesmo. A zato nas svijet ne poznaje što ne poznaje njega.“ Poslanica nastavlja da se još ne očitova što ćemo biti, ali kada se očituje, bit ćemo mu slični, jer ćemo ga gledati kao što jest. Tko god ima tu nadu, čisti se kao što je on čist.

Vladimir Grebenar u tome vidi **obećanje da će vjernici biti Bogu slični** i da ih čeka budućnost, vječnost „kakvu ne možemo zamisliti“. Opisuje osobni doživljaj te neizvjesnosti: osjeća uzbuđenje i izazov, jer nitko na zemlji ne zna što je Bog pripremio. Podsjeća da Sveto pismo govori kako je Bog onima koji ustraju do spasenja pripremio „što oko nije vidjelo, što uho nije čulo“.

„Silno se radujem da se to dogodi“, kaže voditelj. Evanđelje je radosna vijest, a tko se može radovati Božjoj riječi, prema njegovim riječima, na dobrom je putu, jer je „već sad zakoračio u vječnost“.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje je uglavnom usklađeno s Prvom Ivanovom poslanicom: vjernici su već sada Božja djeca, a u budućem gledanju Boga bit će mu slični. Potrebno je samo pojasniti da ta sličnost znači preobrazbu i zajedništvo s Bogom po milosti, a ne postajanje Bogom po naravi, te da radost zbog Božje riječi sama po sebi nije jamstvo spasenja.
concerns: Izraz „bit ćemo Bogu slični” treba tumačiti kao sudjelovanje u Božjem životu i preobrazbu po milosti, a ne kao stjecanje božanske biti; poslanica govori o gledanju Boga i sličnosti s njim.
Tvrdnju da je onaj tko se raduje Božjoj riječi „na dobrom putu” treba shvatiti kao ohrabrenje, ne kao dovoljan dokaz ili jamstvo spasenja. Sama poslanica povezuje nadu u Boga s čišćenjem života.
magisterium.enrichment: Prva Ivanova poslanica spaja sadašnje dostojanstvo Božje djece s budućom nadom: još ne znamo u punini što ćemo biti, ali ta nada usmjerava vjernika prema svetosti. Kršćanska vječnost nije samo neodređena budućnost nego blaženo zajedništvo s Bogom, koje svoju puninu uključuje i u uskrsnuću tijela.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation is mostly aligned with the First Epistle of John: believers are already now children of God, and in the future seeing of God they will be like him. It is only necessary to clarify that this likeness means transformation and communion with God by grace, and not becoming God by nature, and that joy over the word of God in itself is not a guarantee of salvation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The First Epistle of John combines the present dignity of the children of God with future hope: we do not yet know in fullness what we will be, but that hope directs the believer toward holiness. Christian eternity is not merely an indeterminate future, but blessed communion with God, which includes its fullness also in the resurrection of the body.
concerns_en: The expression "we will be like God" should be interpreted as participation in divine life and transformation by grace, rather than as acquiring the divine essence; the epistle speaks of seeing God and being like him.

The claim that whoever rejoices in God's word is "on the right path" should be taken as encouragement, not as sufficient proof or a guarantee of salvation. The epistle itself connects hope in God with the purification of life.

sections.subtitle_en: „We are called children of God, and so we are“: excitement before uncertain eternity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar speaks with joy about eternity prepared by God
sections.content_en:
The second reading is taken from the **First Epistle of John**: „Beloved, see what love the Father has bestowed on us, that we may be called the children of God; and so we are. The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him.“ The Epistle continues that it has not yet been revealed what we shall be, but when it is revealed, we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is. Everyone who has this hope purifies himself, just as he is pure.

Vladimir Grebenar sees in this **a promise that believers will be like God** and that a future, an eternity awaits them „such as we cannot imagine“. He describes a personal experience of that uncertainty: he feels excitement and challenge, because no one on earth knows what God has prepared. He reminds that Sacred Scripture speaks of how God has prepared for those who persevere until salvation „what no eye has seen, what no ear has heard“.

„I rejoice immensely that this will happen“, says the host. The gospel is good news, and whoever can rejoice in God's word, according to his words, is on the right path, because he has „already now stepped into eternity“.

sections.subtitle: Blaženstva s gore i Isus koji je govorio bez mikrofona
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj uspoređuje Isusovo propovijedanje na gori sa svojim nastupima na promocijama s mikrofonom i bez njega
sections.content:
Evanđelje svetkovine donosi Isusova **blaženstva**. Ugledavši mnoštvo, Isus se uspinje na goru, sjeda i počinje poučavati učenike:

- Blago siromasima duhom, njihovo je kraljevstvo nebesko.
- Blago ožalošćenima, oni će se utješiti.
- Blago krotkima, oni će baštiniti zemlju.
- Blago gladnima i žednima pravednosti, oni će se nasititi.
- Blago milosrdnima, oni će zadobiti milosrđe.
- Blago čistima srcem, oni će Boga gledati.
- Blago mirotvorcima, oni će se sinovima Božjim zvati.
- Blago progonjenima zbog pravednosti, njihovo je kraljevstvo nebesko.
- Blago vama kad vas zbog mene pogrde i prognaju i sve zlo slažu protiv vas.

Odlomak završava riječima kojima je i otvorena emisija: „Radujte se i kličite, velika je plaća vaša na nebesima.“

Vladimir Grebenar u tumačenju polazi od naizgled sporednog detalja: Isus je na gori govorio **bez mikrofona i zvučnika**. Uspoređuje to sa svojim iskustvom s promocija na kojima trenutačno nastupa. S mikrofonom ga svi lijepo čuju i ne mora vikati, a Isus je, kaže, morao vikati.

Iz vlastitog iskustva zaključuje da je poruka izgovorena bez mikrofona snažnija i nosi veće pomazanje, „zato što je autentično“. S mikrofonom se može govoriti „iz glave, iz racija“ i čitati unaprijed napisan govor. Bez mikrofona napisani govor nije moguće čitati, pa se, želi li se održati dobar govor, mora govoriti iz srca. Voditelj pritom pojašnjava da to ne znači da ne govori iz srca kada koristi mikrofon, ali bez njega, kaže, „sigurno“ govori iz srca.

magisterium.assessment: Nabrajanje Blaženstava i njihovo predstavljanje kao središnjeg Isusova nauka u skladu je s Evanđeljem i katoličkim naukom: Blaženstva usmjeravaju čovjeka prema Kraljevstvu nebeskom i oblikuju Isusov poziv na život. Međutim, tvrdnje da je Isus morao vikati te da govor bez mikrofona nosi veće pomazanje zato što je autentičniji nisu utemeljene u navedenom evanđeoskom izvještaju i mogu pogrešno povezati djelovanje Duha ili iskrenost s uporabom određene tehnologije.
concerns: Evanđelje govori o Isusovu poučavanju na gori, ali ne navodi da je govorio bez mikrofona ni da je morao vikati; takve su tvrdnje nagađanje, a ne biblijski podatak.

Sugestija da govor bez mikrofona „sigurno“ dolazi iz srca i ima veće pomazanje pretjerana je: autentičnost i duhovna plodnost ne ovise same po sebi o tome govori li netko uz mikrofon ili prema pripremljenom tekstu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ističe da su Blaženstva u srcu Isusova propovijedanja i da obećanja Božjega Kraljevstva povezuju s konkretnim oblikom života učenika. Njihova se snaga očituje u nasljedovanju Krista i životu po evanđeoskim krepostima, a ne u određenom načinu ozvučenja ili izlaganja.

magisterium.assessment_en: Enumerating the Beatitudes and presenting them as the central teaching of Jesus is in accordance with the Gospel and Catholic teaching: the Beatitudes direct man toward the Kingdom of heaven and form Jesus' call to life. However, claims that Jesus had to shout and that speaking without a microphone carries a greater anointing because it is more authentic are not grounded in the cited gospel account and may erroneously connect the action of the Spirit or sincerity with the use of a specific technology.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching emphasizes that the Beatitudes are at the heart of Jesus' preaching and that they connect the promises of the Kingdom of God with the concrete form of life of disciples. Their power is manifested in following Christ and living according to evangelical virtues, and not in a specific method of sound amplification or presentation.
concerns_en: The Gospel speaks of Jesus' teaching on the mountain, but does not state that he spoke without a microphone or that he had to shout; such claims are speculation, not biblical data.

The suggestion that speaking without a microphone "surely" comes from the heart and has a greater anointing is exaggerated: authenticity and spiritual fruitfulness do not in themselves depend on whether someone speaks with a microphone or according to a prepared text.

sections.subtitle_en: The Beatitudes from the mount and Jesus who spoke without a microphone
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host compares Jesus' preaching on the mount with his own appearances at book presentations with and without a microphone
sections.content_en:
The gospel of the solemnity presents Jesus' **Beatitudes**. Seeing the multitudes, Jesus goes up on a mountain, sits down, and begins to teach his disciples:

- Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
- Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
- Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.
- Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.
- Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
- Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
- Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.
- Blessed are those who are persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
- Blessed are you when they revile and persecute you and utter all kinds of evil against you falsely on my account.

The passage concludes with the words with which the broadcast was opened: „Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven.“

In his interpretation Vladimir Grebenar starts from a seemingly secondary detail: Jesus on the mountain spoke **without a microphone and loudspeakers**. He compares this with his own experience from book presentations where he currently performs. With a microphone everyone hears him nicely and he does not have to shout, whereas Jesus, he says, had to shout.

From his own experience he concludes that a message spoken without a microphone is stronger and carries greater anointing, „because it is authentic“. With a microphone one can speak „from the head, from reason“ and read a pre-written speech. Without a microphone it is not possible to read a written speech, so, if one wants to give a good speech, one must speak from the heart. The host clarifies that this does not mean he does not speak from the heart when using a microphone, but without it, he says, he „certainly“ speaks from the heart.

sections.subtitle: Blaženstva kao put spasenja i poziv na osobno razmatranje
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva slušatelje da u molitvi razmatraju blaženstva
sections.content:
Vraćajući se sadržaju evanđelja, Vladimir Grebenar ističe da Isus blaženstvo izriče **onima koji se spašavaju**: koji postižu spasenje, kojima se otvaraju vrata vječnosti, koji su daleko od propasti i koji ostavljaju prošlost iza sebe te se okreću budućnosti.

Umjesto da blaženstva redom tumači, voditelj slušateljima prepušta osobni rad: Gospodin je blaženstva redom nabrojao, a poziv je na svakome da uđe u molitvu i razmatra ono što piše. Izražava uvjerenje da će Gospodin svakome koji to učini „dati riječ u srce“, osobito na dan tako velike svetkovine.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na molitvu i osobno razmatranje Blaženstava dobro je usklađen s kršćanskim čitanjem Svetoga pisma, a njihovo usmjerenje prema nebeskom Kraljevstvu i vječnoj blaženosti ima čvrstu katoličku osnovu. Ipak, izraz da se blaženstvo izriče onima „koji postižu spasenje“ može zvučati kao da se spasenje zaslužuje vlastitim trudom, pa bi trebalo jasnije reći da se Blaženstva žive kao odgovor na Božju milost.
concerns: Izraz „postižu spasenje“ ne objašnjava odnos Božje milosti i ljudskog odgovora te bi se mogao protumačiti pelagijanski, premda sam odlomak izričito ne tvrdi da se spasenje zaslužuje bez milosti.
Osobno razmatranje je korisno, ali nije zamjena za cjelovito tumačenje: Blaženstva sadrže konkretne pozive na milosrđe, čistoću srca, pravednost i mir.
magisterium.enrichment: Blaženstva nisu samo obećanje nagrade u budućnosti nego i put učeništva koji se živi već sada, premda se njegova punina ostvaruje u vječnom zajedništvu s Bogom. Crkveni prikaz izričito povezuje življenje Blaženstava s Božjom milošću i opisuje ga kao čovjekov odgovor ljubavi na Božji savez; osobna molitva zato je plodna kada vodi i konkretnom životu po njima.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to prayer and personal meditation on the Beatitudes is well aligned with the Christian reading of Sacred Scripture, and their orientation toward the heavenly Kingdom and eternal beatitude has a firm Catholic foundation. Nevertheless, the expression that beatitude is pronounced upon those "who attain salvation" can sound as though salvation is earned by one's own effort, so it should be stated more clearly that the Beatitudes are lived as a response to God's grace.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Beatitudes are not only a promise of reward in the future, but also a path of discipleship that is lived already now, although its fullness is realized in eternal communion with God. The ecclesial portrayal explicitly connects living the Beatitudes with God's grace and describes it as man's response of love to God's covenant; personal prayer is therefore fruitful when it also leads to concrete living according to them.
concerns_en: The expression "attain salvation" does not explain the relationship between God's grace and human response and could be interpreted in a Pelagian manner, although the passage itself does not explicitly claim that salvation is earned without grace.
Personal meditation is useful, but it is not a substitute for a comprehensive interpretation: the Beatitudes contain concrete calls to mercy, purity of heart, justice, and peace.

sections.subtitle_en: The Beatitudes as the path of salvation and a call to personal contemplation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invites listeners to contemplate the Beatitudes in prayer
sections.content_en:
Returning to the content of the gospel, Vladimir Grebenar emphasizes that Jesus pronounces blessedness upon **those who are being saved**: who achieve salvation, to whom the doors of eternity are opened, who are far from destruction, and who leave the past behind them and turn toward the future.

Instead of interpreting the Beatitudes one by one, the host leaves personal work to the listeners: the Lord listed the Beatitudes in order, and the invitation is for everyone to enter into prayer and contemplate what is written. He expresses conviction that the Lord will „give a word into the heart“ of everyone who does so, especially on the day of such a great solemnity.

sections.subtitle: Svi sveti kao svetkovina Crkve: slavlje onoga čemu vjernici teže
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar objašnjava zašto svetkovinu Svih svetih smatra svetkovinom Crkve

magisterium.assessment: Dobro ističe svetost kao cilj kršćanskog života i zajedništvo svetih kao zajedništvo Crkve, koje povezuje vjernike na zemlji s onima koji su preminuli u Kristu. Ipak, tvrdnja da su Isus, Marija i Duh Sveti „glava Crkve” teološki je netočna: Krist je Glava Crkve, dok je Marija njezina osobito povlaštena članica i Majka, a Duh Sveti njezin životvorni dar.
concerns: Izjednačavanje Isusa, Marije i Duha Svetoga kao glave Crkve zamagljuje bitnu razliku između Kristova jedinstvenog položaja Glave i Marijina položaja u zajedništvu svetih.

Opis svetkovine kao slavlja „onoga čemu mi težimo” može biti neprecizan ako se time sugerira da su svi vjernici koji još hode zemljom već sveci u smislu onih koji su postigli nebesku slavu. Svetkovina ponajprije časti sve svete, poznate i nepoznate, a ujedno potiče vjernike na svetost.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva je zajedništvo svetih i Kristovo Tijelo: Krist je Glava, a vjernici su udovi povezani vjerom i krštenjem, pri čemu ta povezanost ne prestaje smrću. Svetost nije ljudsko postignuće neovisno o Bogu, nego dar milosti po Kristu, kojemu svi vjernici teže životom ljubavi i nasljedovanjem evanđelja.

magisterium.assessment_en: It rightly highlights holiness as the goal of Christian life and the communion of saints as the communion of the Church, which unites believers on earth with those who have fallen asleep in Christ. Nevertheless, the claim that Jesus, Mary, and the Holy Spirit are the "head of the Church" is theologically inaccurate: Christ is the Head of the Church, while Mary is its particularly privileged member and Mother, and the Holy Spirit is its life-giving gift.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church is the communion of saints and the Body of Christ: Christ is the Head, and believers are members joined by faith and baptism, with this connection not ceasing in death. Holiness is not a human achievement independent of God, but a gift of grace through Christ, toward which all believers strive by a life of love and imitation of the gospel.
concerns_en: Equating Jesus, Mary, and the Holy Spirit as the head of the Church obscures the essential distinction between Christ's unique position as Head and Mary's position in the communion of saints.

Describing the solemnity as a celebration of "what we strive for" can be imprecise if it thereby suggests that all believers who still walk the earth are already saints in the sense of those who have attained heavenly glory. The solemnity primarily honors all saints, known and unknown, and at the same time encourages believers toward holiness.

sections.subtitle: Nije Dušni dan, nego dan radosti: obiteljsko slavlje po uzoru na „slavu“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predlaže da katoličke obitelji slave Sve svete kao svoju svetkovinu
sections.content:
Vladimir Grebenar upozorava na raširenu zabunu. Ljudi na ovaj dan obično odlaze na groblje, ali to je, podsjeća, **Dušni dan**, koji se slavi sutradan. Svi sveti trebali bi biti dan **velike radosti**, s prekrasnim ručkom i obitelji na okupu.

Obitelji posvećene Bogu, prema njegovim riječima, trebale bi toga dana slaviti svoju svetkovinu. Kao usporedbu navodi pravoslavni običaj **slave**: obitelj izabere sveca zaštitnika i na njegov dan slavi. Na isti bi način, smatra voditelj, svi katolici trebali častiti i slaviti Sve svete, „jer to je, braćo i sestre, naša slava“.

Tumačenje zaključuje rečenicom: „Bog je proslavio svete zato što su oni proslavljali njega.“

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno razlikuje svetkovinu Svih svetih od spomen-dana svih vjernika pokojnih i naglašava radost prikladnu slavljenju svetih. No pretjerano je prikazati odlazak na groblje kao nešto što pripada isključno Dušnom danu: Crkva povezuje oba dana, a posjet groblju i molitva za pokojne mogu se događati i na svetkovinu Svih svetih; radost pritom ne isključuje žalost ni sjećanje.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je odlazak na groblje „Dušni dan” može navesti na pogrešno shvaćanje, jer se pokojnih i groblja vjernici spominju i na svetkovinu Svih svetih.

Predstavljanje obiteljskog ručka i slavljenja po uzoru na pravoslavnu slavu kao nečega što bi „svi katolici trebali” činiti iznosi osobni ili kulturni prijedlog kao opću katoličku obvezu, za što ovdje nema osnove.
Naglasak na radosti treba razumjeti zajedno s dopuštenom i prirodnom tugom zbog pokojnih; liturgijska radost ne zahtijeva da obiteljsko sjećanje ili žalovanje budu potisnuti.
magisterium.enrichment: Svetkovina Svih svetih slavi nebrojeno mnoštvo svetih i potiče vjernike da slijede njihov primjer, dok se Dušni dan posebno posvećuje molitvenom spomenu svih vjernika pokojnih. Ipak, ta su slavlja povezana: liturgijski poziv na radost može se sjediniti s tugom i sjećanjem, a zajedništvo Crkve obuhvaća i žive i one koji su preminuli. Rečenica da je Bog proslavio svete jer su oni proslavljali njega može se prihvatiti ako se pritom jasno kaže da njihova svetost i spasenje počivaju na Božjoj milosti po Kristu.

citations.document_title: 1 November 1983: Celebration of Mass at the Roman cemetery of Verano on the Solemnity of All Saints - Homily
1 November 1985: Eucharistic concelebration at the Roman cemetery of Verano on the Solemnity of All Saints - Homily

magisterium.assessment_en: It correctly distinguishes the Solemnity of All Saints from the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed and emphasizes the joy appropriate to celebrating the saints. But it is exaggerated to present going to the cemetery as something that belongs exclusively to All Souls' Day: the Church connects both days, and visiting the cemetery and praying for the deceased can also take place on the Solemnity of All Saints; joy in doing so does not exclude sorrow or remembrance.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Solemnity of All Saints celebrates the innumerable multitude of saints and encourages believers to follow their example, while All Souls' Day is especially dedicated to the prayerful remembrance of all the faithful departed. Nevertheless, these celebrations are connected: the liturgical call to joy can unite with grief and remembrance, and the communion of the Church encompasses both the living and those who have passed away. The sentence that God glorified the saints because they glorified him can be accepted if it is clearly stated that their holiness and salvation rest on God's grace through Christ.
concerns_en: The claim that going to the cemetery is "All Souls' Day" may lead to a misconception, because believers also commemorate the deceased and visit cemeteries on the Solemnity of All Saints.

Presenting a family lunch and celebration modelled on the Orthodox slava as something that "all Catholics should" do sets forth a personal or cultural proposal as a general Catholic obligation, for which there is no basis here.
The emphasis on joy should be understood together with permitted and natural grief for the deceased; liturgical joy does not require that family remembrance or mourning be suppressed.

sections.subtitle_en: Not All Souls' Day, but a day of joy: family celebration modeled on „slava“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host proposes that Catholic families celebrate All Saints as their solemnity
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar warns of a widespread confusion. People usually visit cemeteries on this day, but that is, he recalls, **All Souls' Day**, which is celebrated the next day. All Saints should be a day of **great joy**, with a wonderful lunch and family gathered together.

Families consecrated to God, according to his words, should celebrate their solemnity on that day. As a comparison he cites the Orthodox custom of **slava**: a family chooses a patron saint and celebrates on his day. In the same way, the host believes, all Catholics should venerate and celebrate All Saints, „because that, brothers and sisters, is our slava“.

He concludes the interpretation with the sentence: „God glorified the saints because they glorified him.“

sections.subtitle: Turneja knjige „Isus Lider“ (treći dio): od Biograda do Nove Gradiške
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje raspored promocija knjige Isus Lider, treći dio
sections.content:
Nakon tumačenja Vladimir Grebenar poziva na promocije knjige **„Isus Lider“, treći dio**, s podnaslovom **„Kako spriječiti razorne demonske utjecaje?“**. Raspored predstavljanja je sljedeći:

- **ponedjeljak, 2. studenoga**: Biograd na Moru, hotel Ilirija, Tina Ujevića 7
- **utorak, 3. studenoga**: Solin, hotel President Solin
- **srijeda, 4. studenoga**: Imotski, Pučko otvoreno učilište Imotski
- **utorak, 10. studenoga**: Valpovo, vila Valpovo
- **srijeda, 11. studenoga**: Nova Gradiška, centar kompetencija Nova Gradiška

Voditelj napominje da je to zasad sve te da će naknadno objaviti raspored za idući dio turneje.

magisterium.assessment: Ovaj odlomak uglavnom je organizacijska najava, pa ne iznosi dovoljno teološkog sadržaja da bi se mogla procijeniti usklađenost knjige s katoličkim naukom. Samo isticanje demonskih utjecaja nije protivno vjeri, ali naslov ne pokazuje poštuje li knjiga potrebnu razboritost u razlikovanju duhovne kušnje od drugih uzroka zla.
concerns: Iz samog naslova nije moguće zaključiti pripisuje li knjiga konkretne teškoće demonima bez dostatnih razloga ili na senzacionalistički način; za takvo je razlučivanje potrebna kritička procjena i razboritost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera priznaje stvarnost Sotone i njegovu sposobnost da ljude navodi na zlo, ali ujedno odbacuje olako pripisivanje svakog zla izravnom demonskom djelovanju. Zato je važna ravnoteža: kršćanin treba biti budan i oslanjati se na molitvu, ali ne zanemarivati ljudsku slobodu niti razborito ispitivanje okolnosti.

citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: This passage is primarily an organizational announcement, so it does not present enough theological content to assess the book's alignment with Catholic teaching. Emphasizing demonic influences alone is not contrary to faith, but the title does not show whether the book observes the necessary prudence in distinguishing spiritual temptation from other causes of evil.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith recognizes the reality of Satan and his ability to lead people into evil, but at the same time rejects lightly attributing every evil to direct demonic action. Therefore, balance is important: a Christian should be vigilant and rely on prayer, but not neglect human freedom or the prudent examination of circumstances.
concerns_en: From the title alone it is not possible to conclude whether the book attributes concrete difficulties to demons without sufficient reasons or in a sensationalist manner; critical assessment and prudence are necessary for such discernment.

sections.subtitle: „Nisam uzeo ni jedan cent“: odgovor na klevete o donacijama
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar odlučno odbacuje optužbe da uzima novac od donacija inicijative Ora et Labora

magisterium.assessment: Naglašavanje transparentnosti, volonterskog rada i namjenskog korištenja donacija načelno je spojivo s kršćanskom odgovornošću, ali iz odlomka nije moguće provjeriti istinitost tih tvrdnji. Teološki je problematično kritičare unaprijed označiti kao ljude preko kojih djeluje Sotona i slušatelje poticati da njihove primjedbe nazovu klevetom bez razmatranja dokaza, jer to može poticati brzoplet sud i nepravedno narušiti nečiji ugled.
concerns: Pripisivanje kritičara Sotoninu djelovanju iznosi ozbiljnu procjenu njihovih motiva bez prikazane provjere; kršćansko vjerovanje u zlo ne opravdava automatski takvo pripisivanje pojedincima.
Izraz „kleveta” opravdan je samo ako su optužbe doista lažne i nepravedno štete ugledu; sam odlomak ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se to utvrdilo.

Pozivanje na predaju protivnika Božjem sudu može se razumjeti kao prepuštanje konačnog suda Bogu, ali ne bi smjelo zamijeniti istinoljubiv odgovor, razborito razjašnjenje činjenica i poziv na pomirenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija potvrđuje da Sotona djeluje u svijetu, ali istodobno upozorava na oprez pri prosuđivanju konkretnog demonskog djelovanja te na očuvanje ljudske slobode i odgovornosti. Isusov poziv da ljubimo neprijatelje i ne osuđujemo podsjeća da se obrana od neistinite optužbe može spojiti s milosrđem i suzdržanošću u sudu o osobama.

citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: Emphasizing transparency, volunteer work, and the targeted use of donations is in principle compatible with Christian responsibility, but from the passage it is not possible to verify the truth of these claims. It is theologically problematic to label critics in advance as people through whom Satan acts and to encourage listeners to call their remarks slander without considering evidence, as this can foster rash judgment and unjustly damage someone's reputation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition confirms that Satan acts in the world, but at the same time warns of caution when discerning concrete demonic action and of preserving human freedom and responsibility. Jesus' call to love enemies and not judge reminds us that defense against an untrue accusation can be combined with mercy and restraint in judging persons.
concerns_en: Attributing critics to Satan's action presents a serious judgment of their motives without demonstrated verification; Christian belief in evil does not automatically justify such attribution to individuals.
The term "slander" is justified only if the accusations are indeed false and unjustly damage reputation; the passage itself does not provide sufficient data to determine this.

Invoking handing opponents over to God's judgment can be understood as leaving final judgment to God, but it should not replace a truthful answer, prudent clarification of facts, and a call to reconciliation.

sections.subtitle: Završni blagoslov
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zaključuje emisiju završnim blagoslovom
sections.content:
Emisiju za svetkovinu Svih svetih Vladimir Grebenar zatvara tradicionalnim blagoslovom: „Neka se sveta Mati sa svojim Sinom i svetim Josipom udostoji blagoslov svoj nam dati, u ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga. Amen.“

Time završava epizoda u kojoj su se izmjenjivali molitva, tumačenje Otkrivenja, Prve Ivanove poslanice i blaženstava, osobno svjedočanstvo o viđenju četiriju anđela, poziv hrvatskom narodu na „Božji ustanak“ te obavijesti o radu inicijative Ora et Labora.

magisterium.assessment: Završna molitva uglavnom je usklađena s katoličkom pobožnošću: zazivanje Marije i svetoga Josipa da zagovaraju vjernike uobičajeno je unutar zajedništva svetih. Izraz da oni daju „svoj blagoslov” može biti nejasan ako bi se shvatio kao da blagoslivljaju neovisno o Bogu, ali u molitvenom kontekstu može se razumjeti kao zaziv njihova zagovora i pomoći.
concerns: Bilo bi teološki jasnije naglasiti da je Bog izvor svakoga blagoslova, a da Marija i sveti Josip za nas zagovaraju njegovu milost; dostupni opis ne pokazuje da je govornik namjeravao pripisati im neovisnu božansku moć.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička molitva smije tražiti zagovor svetaca: oni nisu predmet štovanja kao Bog, nego članovi zajedništva svetih kojima se vjernici obraćaju kao zagovornicima pred Bogom. Crkvene molitve izričito mole da se blagoslov primi po zagovoru Blažene Djevice ili nekoga svetca, dok se blagoslov u trinitarnom obrascu pripisuje svemogućem Bogu.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 2 February 2022 - Catechesis on Saint Joseph: 10. Saint Joseph and the communion of saints

magisterium.assessment_en: The concluding prayer is mostly aligned with Catholic devotion: invoking Mary and Saint Joseph to intercede for believers is common within the communion of saints. The expression that they give "their blessing" can be ambiguous if understood as though they bless independently of God, but in a prayerful context it can be understood as an invocation of their intercession and help.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic prayer may ask for the intercession of the saints: they are not the object of adoration like God, but members of the communion of saints whom believers address as intercessors before God. Church prayers explicitly pray that a blessing be received through the intercession of the Blessed Virgin or a saint, while blessing in the Trinitarian formula is attributed to Almighty God.
concerns_en: It would be theologically clearer to emphasize that God is the source of every blessing, and that Mary and Saint Joseph intercede for his grace for us; the available description does not show that the speaker intended to attribute independent divine power to them.

sections.subtitle_en: Concluding blessing
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host concludes the broadcast with a final blessing
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar closes the program for the solemnity of All Saints with a traditional blessing: „May the holy Mother with her Son and Saint Joseph deign to give us their blessing, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.“

With that ends an episode in which prayer, interpretation of Revelation, the First Epistle of John, and the Beatitudes, personal testimony of a vision of four angels, a call to the Croatian people for a „God's uprising“, and notices about the work of the Ora et Labora initiative alternated.

iterations.theme_en: Interpretation of the holy word for the solemnity of All Saints, and announcements and notices of the Ora et Labora initiative
